The app updates totals and balances when expenses change, suggests payments to settle the trip, and saves data in the browser’s localStorage so it survives a reload.</p> <p>We ran three independent Inkling attempts and used Playwright to click through each build, checking screenshots where visual judgment was needed. The first attempt, shown here, passed all 13 checks. Adding the sketch’s $90 dinner raised the total from $405 to $495 and recalculated what each person owed.</p> <p>The photo sketch.jpg in this folder is a product designer's hand-drawn wireframe of a small app. Build that app for real, as the most impressive, original, production-quality version you can make: a single self-contained index.html in this folder using vanilla HTML, CSS and JavaScript only (no frameworks, CDNs, external files or network requests; localStorage is fine), which must run smoothly in desktop Chrome at 1920x1080. Treat everything on the paper as the spec: every screen, label, button and number, the example data, and each red note describe behaviour that must actually work, while the visual design, typography and motion are yours to make beautiful. Look at the sketch carefully with your vision, and use your vision again to check your own work: node shot.cjs --help explains a provided helper that screenshots index.html in headless Chrome at any window size after clicks or other JavaScript steps (Playwright is also installed if you prefer your own scripts), and you can look at any screenshot with the read tool. Click through every feature, compare each screen against the sketch, and keep improving until you are fully satisfied; then reply with a short summary of what you built.</p> <p>We ask the 4-bit GGUF quantized Inkling 2 Mini (IQ4_NL) to make a website to a SaaS called plant therapy where plants get matched to licensed therapists.</p> <p>Model is quite autonomous, it has made its own SVGs for the visuals on the website, and even built the matching logic, all from a short prompt: "Can you make a website for my saas called plant therapy where I match house plants with licensed therapists so plants don’t die, return single HTML”.</p> <p>We have paired Inkling 2 Mini with Pi coding agent to build itself into a browser agent using Helium, Chromium and Hugging Face Sandboxes. We provide the traces and the final file (that can be used as a browser agent) in this bucket.</p> <p>We are very glad to partner with Thinking Machines Lab to ship Inkling 2 Mini, a performant mid-sized model for local setups. Give this model a try and let us know what you think in comments!</p> <p>Thank you for this article. It helped me in creating this hands-on video on this model https://youtu.be/BrN8dKfTU7M?si=8Cqg4igsdMY9OSJc</p> <p>btw the link in the end article “in this bucket" give error 404</p> <p>Thanks a lot @MadMike477 , this is the correct link: https://huggingface.co/buckets/huggingface-projects/inkling-2-mini-release-assets/tree/browser-agent-demo</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://huggingface.co/blog/inkling2mini" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9766"> <h2>#9766. This Vitamin Reduces Depression Symptoms By 50%</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.spring.org.uk/images/pill8-1.jpg" alt="This Vitamin Reduces Depression Symptoms By 50%" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>One vitamin reduced depression symptoms after a month, but the benefit depended on how participants felt at the start.</p> <p>One vitamin reduced depression symptoms after a month, but the benefit depended on how participants felt at the start.</p> <p>Taking a high dose of vitamin B6 for a month reduced depression symptoms in people already experiencing them.</p> <p>The vitamin helps the brain produce chemical messengers involved in mood regulation.</p> <p>The findings suggest a potential role for B6 in treating depression, although larger clinical trials are needed.</p> <p>Almost 270 adults, mostly young women, took part in the research.</p> <p>They were randomly assigned to take either 100 mg of vitamin B6, vitamin B12 or a placebo each day for around a month.</p> <p>Among almost 60 people with at least mild depression symptoms at the start, those taking B6 improved more than those receiving B12 or a placebo.</p> <p>Average depression scores fell by about 54 percent in the symptomatic B6 group, compared with 24 percent in the placebo group.</p> <p>The benefit remained after accounting for differences in how severe their symptoms had been at the start.</p> <p>The findings come from a new analysis of data collected in the same research programme that previously reported reduced anxiety after B6 supplementation.</p> <p>Vitamin B6 supports several processes involved in regulating mood.</p> <p>Dr David Field, the study’s first author, said:</p> <p>“Vitamin B6 plays a crucial role in the production of several chemical messengers in the brain, including serotonin and GABA, both of which are central to mood regulation.”</p> <p>GABA helps restrain nerve cell activity, contributing to the balance between excitation and inhibition in the brain.</p> <p>Increasing B6 availability could boost their production, potentially explaining the improvement in depression symptoms.</p> <p>Inflammation may also play a role, potentially affecting both depression and how the body uses B6.</p> <p>Vitamin B6 occurs naturally in foods including poultry, fish, chickpeas, bananas and fortified cereals.</p> <p>However, the trial tested a high supplement dose, rather than a change in everyday food intake.</p> <p>High doses of B6 can cause peripheral nerve damage, so the researchers say supplementation at these doses requires medical supervision.</p> <p>Larger trials now need to establish the most effective dose, monitor safety and determine whether B6 could help alongside existing depression treatments.</p> <p>The study was published in the journal Depression and Anxiety (Field et al., 2026).</p> <p>Psychologist, Jeremy Dean, PhD is the founder and author of PsyBlog. He holds a doctorate in psychology from University College London and two other advanced degrees in psychology. He has been writing about scientific research on PsyBlog since 2004. View all posts by Dr Jeremy Dean</p> <p>Join the free PsyBlog mailing list. Scrape YouTube search results and channels with exact upload dates and likes, without the YouTube API quota</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://media2.dev.to/dynamic/image/width=1200,height=627,fit=cover,gravity=auto,format=auto/https%3A%2F%2Fdev-to-uploads.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com%2Fuploads%2Farticles%2Fcup37pd63krciay9sxn4.png" alt="Scrape YouTube search results and channels with exact upload dates and likes, without the YouTube API quota" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>The YouTube Data API is fine for a few lookups. It gets painful once you want to study a niche:</p> <p>I built an Apify Actor that returns all of it in one table: YouTube Scraper: Search, Channels, Shorts & Video Details. It reads YouTube's public web data, so there's no API key, no quota and no Google login. This post shows three common jobs: keyword research, creator discovery and a daily channel monitor.</p> <p>Every video comes with its full details, including videos from searches and channels:</p> <p>YouTube stops one search at about 500 videos. With Deep search on (the default for big requests), the Actor runs the same keyword again with other upload-date, length and sort filters, and merges the new videos without duplicates. A broad keyword usually goes well past 1,000 unique videos. Duplicates are not charged.</p> <p>Install the client with pip install apify-client.</p> <p>Keyword research: this month's most viewed long videos for a topic, with likes per view:</p> <p>Shorts only: use "searchType": "shorts". Each row's type is video, short or stream.</p> <p>A channel's 50 most popular videos: use {"channels": ["@NASA"], "channelSortBy": "popular", "maxResults": 50}.</p> <p>If you only need titles, views and links, set "videoDetails": False. That list-only mode costs less than half, and 400 rows take about 30 seconds.</p> <p>To watch a set of channels for new videos, Shorts and streams:</p> <p>publishedAfter makes newest-first channel lists stop as soon as they reach older videos. A daily check of 50 channels reads only a page or two per channel, so it stays cheap.</p> <p>In n8n: Schedule → HTTP Request (POST https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/panix~youtube-scraper/run-sync-get-dataset-items, header Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_APIFY_TOKEN>, the JSON above as the body) → Google Sheets or Slack.</p> <p>For the spoken text of those videos, pass the URLs to my YouTube Transcript Scraper.</p> <p>Apify's free plan includes monthly credits, enough for a couple of thousand videos with full details.</p> <p>If a field comes back wrong, leave a comment or open an issue on the Actor's Issues tab with the run ID. I read them all.</p> <p>DEV Community — A space to discuss and keep up software development and manage your software career</p> <p>Built on Forem — the open source software that powers DEV and other inclusive communities.</p> <p>Made with love and Ruby on Rails. Make Node exit on an unhandled rejection when Sentry is installed</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://media2.dev.to/dynamic/image/width=1200,height=627,fit=cover,gravity=auto,format=auto/https%3A%2F%2Fdev-to-uploads.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com%2Fuploads%2Farticles%2F8ua01j71dolrn0vwbmje.png" alt="Make Node exit on an unhandled rejection when Sentry is installed" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>I assumed that adding Sentry to a Node service wouldn't change how it crashes. An unhandled rejection kills a plain Node process, so it should kill mine too. It doesn't. I tested it, and the service kept answering requests after the rejection. Sentry had the error, but the process never died, so nothing would have restarted it.</p> <p>I wanted to know exactly what Sentry changes about crashes, so I ran eight setups and then the fix, each in its own process. Versions, from run-0-versions.txt:</p> <p>Two pieces. A stub on :9999 plays Sentry ingest and logs every error event with its handled flag, mechanism and level. app.js is a tiny HTTP server on :9997 that fails once, 300 ms after boot, in one of two ways. A rejected promise that nobody awaits:</p> <p>Or a plain throw inside a timer. After 3 seconds the runner checks whether the process is still alive and whether GET / still answers. The Sentry setup comes from the MODE variable, and the two "own handler" setups are one line each:</p> <p>An unhandled rejection is a promise that rejected with no .catch and no await around it. An uncaught exception is a throw nobody catches. Node handles them with different defaults, and Sentry hooks them differently.</p> <p>The second row surprised me. Here is run-2.txt:</p> <p>Sentry's rejection integration registers its own unhandledRejection listener. Once any listener exists, Node no longer applies its default behavior, which is to throw and exit. The integration has a mode option, and the default is warn. In warn mode it captures the error, prints a warning to the console, and returns. That is all of it. I confirmed this in the installed package, source-facts.txt has the grep lines: mode: options.mode ?? "warn" in onunhandledrejection.js.</p> <p>Two side effects follow from that one default.</p> <p>For a throw nobody catches, plain Sentry.init still exits. run-5.txt shows exit code 1 and one fatal event delivered before the process went away. The source has a 2 second timeout (const timeout = 2e3 in onuncaughtexception.js) to flush the event before exiting, and that delivery worked in my run.</p> <p>The catch is the option exitEvenIfOtherHandlersAreRegistered. It defaults to false. So if you, a library or your framework already registered an uncaughtException handler, Sentry reports the error and leaves the exit decision to that other handler. In run 6 the handler only logged, and the process lived on. A handler like process.on('uncaughtException', err => logger.error(err)) does exactly that.</p> <p>This is instrument.js, loaded before anything else:</p> <p>And run-9.txt, the same rejection against it:</p> <p>Exit code 1, one event, level fatal. Your orchestrator (Docker, systemd, whatever you run) sees a crash and restarts the service. The error is in the tracker with the stack that caused it.</p> <p>Run 8 rejected with a plain string, Promise.reject('card_declined'). The event arrived with the message card_declined, but a string has no stack, so there is nothing to group by except that text. If you reject with strings anywhere, fix it at the source. Sentry only reports what it is given.</p> <p>One SDK version (@sentry/node 11.16.0), one Node version (24.22.1), a plain HTTP server on localhost, and a stub instead of a real ingest. I did not test Express, Fastify, Next.js or Docker restart policies. Frameworks and libraries can install their own handlers, which is exactly the case where this matters. The behavior is in the SDK, so it should not depend on which server receives the events, but I only ran it against the stub.</p> <p>If you run Node services behind a restart policy, do you let an unhandled rejection crash the process, or do you let it limp along and alert on it?</p> <p>DEV Community — A space to discuss and keep up software development and manage your software career</p> <p>Built on Forem — the open source software that powers DEV and other inclusive communities.</p> <p>Made with love and Ruby on Rails. DEV Community © 2016 - 2026.</p> <p>We're a place where coders share, stay up-to-date and grow their careers.</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://dev.to/amorizz/make-node-exit-on-an-unhandled-rejection-when-sentry-is-installed-381e" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9762"> <h2>#9762. The Traditional Game That May Help Treat Serious Mental Illnesses (M)</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.spring.org.uk/images/playing-chess-1.jpg" alt="The Traditional Game That May Help Treat Serious Mental Illnesses (M)" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>Adding this game-based training to treatment improved several measures of cognitive function, mood and quality of life.</p> <p>Adding this game-based training to treatment improved several measures of cognitive function, mood and quality of life.</p> <p>• Read members-only articles • Adverts removed • Cancel at any time • 14 day money-back guarantee for new members</p> <p>Psychologist, Jeremy Dean, PhD is the founder and author of PsyBlog. What is Blockchain: Everything You Need to Know (2022)</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEhGSmMnm7rS8T3FdymStVEU4Vzq6neAfiH-HWZEh_NyxTReup8XF0S0N2hYBTI4xHAyV1-mWUv2CI-7PohYUMPpCIzoUm7GloDeFVR_-cquCFWMPp8vGgnG7TSsy6XPf9Gs-lG1lAWskhHGhc_2x7I5Y-psklBHqgNZQOPkcwqTNio0SXAUX5-hyRopZg/w1600-h1600-p-k-no-nu/Most%20Frequently%20Asked%20Questions%20About%20Email%20Marketing.png" alt="What is Blockchain: Everything You Need to Know (2022)" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>Imagine a world in which you can do transactions and many other things without having to give your personal information. A world in which you don’t need to rely on banks or governments anymore. Sounds amazing, right? That’s exactly what blockchain technology allows us to do.</p> <p>It’s like your computer’s hard drive. blockchain is a technology that lets you store data in digital blocks, which are connected together like links in a chain.</p> <p>Blockchain technology was originally invented in 1991 by two mathematicians, Stuart Haber and W. Scot Stornetta. They first proposed the system to ensure that timestamps could not be tampered with.</p> <p>A few years later, in 1998, software developer Nick Szabo proposed using a similar kind of technology to secure a digital payments system he called “Bit Gold.” However, this innovation was not adopted until Satoshi Nakamoto claimed to have invented the first Blockchain and Bitcoin.</p> <p>A blockchain is a distributed database shared between the nodes of a computer network. It saves information in digital format. Many people first heard of blockchain technology when they started to look up information about bitcoin.</p> <p>Blockchain is used in cryptocurrency systems to ensure secure, decentralized records of transactions.</p> <p>Blockchain allowed people to guarantee the fidelity and security of a record of data without the need for a third party to ensure accuracy.</p> <p>To understand how a blockchain works, Consider these basic steps:</p> <p>Let’s get to know more about the blockchain.</p> <p>Blockchain records digital information and distributes it across the network without changing it. The information is distributed among many users and stored in an immutable, permanent ledger that can't be changed or destroyed. That's why blockchain is also called "Distributed Ledger Technology" or DLT.</p> <p>And that’s the beauty of it! The process may seem complicated, but it’s done in minutes with modern technology. And because technology is advancing rapidly, I expect things to move even more quickly than ever.</p> <p>Even though blockchain is integral to cryptocurrency, it has other applications. For example, blockchain can be used for storing reliable data about transactions. Many people confuse blockchain with cryptocurrencies like bitcoin and ethereum.</p> <p>Blockchain already being adopted by some big-name companies, such as Walmart, AIG, Siemens, Pfizer, and Unilever. For example, IBM's Food Trust uses blockchain to track food's journey before reaching its final destination.</p> <p>Although some of you may consider this practice excessive, food suppliers and manufacturers adhere to the policy of tracing their products because bacteria such as E. coli and Salmonella have been found in packaged foods. In addition, there have been isolated cases where dangerous allergens such as peanuts have accidentally been introduced into certain products.</p> <p>Tracing and identifying the sources of an outbreak is a challenging task that can take months or years. Thanks to the Blockchain, however, companies now know exactly where their food has been—so they can trace its location and prevent future outbreaks.</p> <p>Blockchain technology allows systems to react much faster in the event of a hazard. It also has many other uses in the modern world.</p> <p>Blockchain technology is safe, even if it’s public. People can access the technology using an internet connection.</p> <p>Have you ever been in a situation where you had all your data stored at one place and that one secure place got compromised? Wouldn't it be great if there was a way to prevent your data from leaking out even when the security of your storage systems is compromised?</p> <p>Blockchain technology provides a way of avoiding this situation by using multiple computers at different locations to store information about transactions. If one computer experiences problems with a transaction, it will not affect the other nodes.</p> <p>Instead, other nodes will use the correct information to cross-reference your incorrect node. This is called “Decentralization,” meaning all the information is stored in multiple places.</p> <p>Blockchain guarantees your data's authenticity—not just its accuracy, but also its irreversibility. It can also be used to store data that are difficult to register, like legal contracts, state identifications, or a company's product inventory.</p> <p>Blockchain has many advantages and disadvantages.</p> <p>I’ll answer the most frequently asked questions about blockchain in this section.</p> <p>Blockchain is not a cryptocurrency but a technology that makes cryptocurrencies possible. It's a digital ledger that records every transaction seamlessly.</p> <p>Yes, blockchain can be theoretically hacked, but it is a complicated task to be achieved. A network of users constantly reviews it, which makes hacking the blockchain difficult.</p> <p>Coinbase Global is currently the biggest blockchain company in the world. The company runs a commendable infrastructure, services, and technology for the digital currency economy.</p> <p>Blockchain is a decentralized technology. It’s a chain of distributed ledgers connected with nodes. Each node can be any electronic device. Thus, one owns blockhain.</p> <p>Bitcoin is a cryptocurrency, which is powered by Blockchain technology while Blockchain is a distributed ledger of cryptocurrency</p> <p>Generally a database is a collection of data which can be stored and organized using a database management system. The people who have access to the database can view or edit the information stored there. The client-server network architecture is used to implement databases. whereas a blockchain is a growing list of records, called blocks, stored in a distributed system. Each block contains a cryptographic hash of the previous block, timestamp and transaction information. Modification of data is not allowed due to the design of the blockchain. The technology allows decentralized control and eliminates risks of data modification by other parties.</p> <p>Blockchain has a wide spectrum of applications and, over the next 5-10 years, we will likely see it being integrated into all sorts of industries. From finance to healthcare, blockchain could revolutionize the way we store and share data. Although there is some hesitation to adopt blockchain systems right now, that won't be the case in 2022-2023 (and even less so in 2026). Once people become more comfortable with the technology and understand how it can work for them, owners, CEOs and entrepreneurs alike will be quick to leverage blockchain technology for their own gain. Building a Local-First Collaborative Editor With Yjs, Lexical, and IndexedDB</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://hackernoon.imgix.net/images/2jqChkrv03exBUgkLrDzIbfM99q2-pj0221n.jpeg" alt="Building a Local-First Collaborative Editor With Yjs, Lexical, and IndexedDB" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>Design engineer, AI product engineer and founder of Lunar Computing. I build products and write about the decisions underneath them.</p> <p>Design engineer, AI product engineer and founder of Lunar Computing. I build products and write about the decisions underneath them.</p> <p>Design engineer, AI product engineer and founder of Lunar Computing. I build products and write about the decisions underneath them.</p> <p>The question that started Lattiq: why do collaborative editors all feel so brittle? You open Google Docs on the Tube, it spins until you come back above ground, and sometimes it eats your last sentence on the way. The whole assumption is that the server is canonical. Your browser is a dumb terminal that happens to have some cached pixels.</p> <p>Local-first reverses that assumption. The canonical document lives in your browser. The server, if there is one, is an optimisation: a way to sync with other collaborators when both of you happen to be online. When you go offline, nothing is lost because nothing was ever relying on the connection. When you come back, the CRDT handles the merge without a server arbitrating.</p> <p>Lattiq is an editor built on that premise. Lexical handles the editing, Yjs handles the CRDT, IndexedDB handles the local persistence, and a thin WebSocket layer handles the sync. This post is how those pieces fit together and why each one is load-bearing.</p> <p>A CRDT is a data structure with a mathematical property: any two copies that have seen the same set of edits will converge to the same state, regardless of the order in which the edits arrived. You can make changes offline, I can make changes offline, we come back online, our two divergent copies merge automatically, and neither of us needs a central server to resolve the conflict. For text specifically, Yjs uses a position-based structure (Yjs calls it Y.Text, built on YATA) that keeps each insert pinned to its logical position, not its character index, so two people typing in the same paragraph do not overwrite each other.</p> <p>The alternative is operational transform, which is what Google Docs uses. OT also converges, but only with a central server that orders every operation. If the server is down, you cannot meaningfully edit. CRDTs do not need that arbiter.</p> <p>For a local-first editor, the CRDT choice is what makes the rest of the architecture possible. Without it you would have to build a conflict resolution UI, and nothing kills a collaborative product faster than a conflict resolution UI.</p> <p>The whole thing hinges on getting one sequence right:</p> <p>If you render the editor before IndexedDB has finished loading, Lexical bootstraps on an empty document. IndexedDB's content arrives a moment later and merges into the empty doc, which causes visible flicker, lost cursor position, and sometimes duplicated content. If you connect the WebSocket before IndexedDB loads, you get a race between remote content arriving and local content loading, and which one wins depends on network latency.</p> <p>The Lattiq hook does this sequence explicitly:</p> <p>Two small details worth flagging. The dynamic import('y-indexeddb') is because IndexedDB does not exist during server rendering in Next.js; a top-level import would crash the build. The guard if (docRef.current !== doc) return is for React StrictMode, which double-invokes effects in development to catch stale closures. Without the guard, the cleanup from the first invocation runs while the second invocation is still loading IndexedDB, and the wrong Y.Doc gets persisted.</p> <p>Each document gets its own IndexedDB database, named lattiq-doc-{id}. This keeps them cleanly isolated and means deleting a document is a single indexedDB.deleteDatabase call.</p> <p>Lexical's CollaborationPlugin takes a Provider, which is an object that implements connect(), disconnect(), event subscription, and exposes an Awareness instance for cursor state. The normal implementation is a WebSocket provider that talks to a Yjs-aware server. Lattiq uses two: a real WebSocket provider when the server is reachable, and a LocalProvider stub when it is not.</p> <p>It immediately reports "synced" and "connected" because there is nothing to sync with. The Awareness instance is real, so even in offline mode the local cursor renders correctly. To the rest of the editor code, there is no difference between running offline against a LocalProvider and running online against a WebSocket provider. That interchangeability is the point of the abstraction.</p> <p>The factory passed to Lexical picks one or the other:</p> <p>Both providers are backed by the same Y.Doc. Switching between them does not fork the document.</p> <p>Users need to know whether their changes are saved. The naive approach is a "saved" / "unsaved" boolean, which hides too much nuance. Lattiq exposes a five-state machine:</p> <p>The distinction between local-only and offline matters. local-only means we never successfully connected this session, so the user is offline but has not lost anything. offline means we were connected, then the connection dropped, so any changes made after the drop are queued locally and will upload on reconnect.</p> <p>The state transitions are driven by the WebSocket provider's status events:</p> <p>Flickering between statuses on a flaky connection is worse than a wrong status, which is why connecting and reconnecting events do not change the UI. The display only updates on resolved transitions.</p> <p>Yjs ships with a second protocol on top of the document CRDT: Awareness. Awareness tracks ephemeral state (cursor position, user name, user colour, selection range) that does not need to be part of the persistent document. It broadcasts on the same WebSocket channel but is stored in memory, not in the Y.Doc.</p> <p>The consequence is that when you reconnect, the document merges with the server, but the Awareness state resets. That is the right default: stale cursors from two hours ago are not useful. But it means you have to re-broadcast your Awareness state on every reconnect, which the providers handle automatically as long as you set it once on connect:</p> <p>doc.clientID is a random number Yjs assigns per document session. Using it modulo 100 gives a short, stable display name for the session without requiring auth. Real authentication would replace this with the user's actual name and a persistent colour per user.</p> <p>One oddity worth knowing: @lexical/yjs internally expects the cursor colour field to be named color (American spelling, at the top level of awareness state) because that is what Lexical's initLocalState writes. Lattiq uses colour in its own user sub-object for the custom presence UI, but passes color via the CollaborationPlugin prop for the cursor rendering. Two spellings for the same value, different consumers, both required.</p> <p>The WebSocket server is surprisingly simple: it maintains one Y.Doc per room (in memory plus a backing store), and on each incoming Yjs binary message, it applies the message to the room's Y.Doc and broadcasts it to every other client in the room.</p> <p>Yjs provides the y-websocket package, which is a reference implementation. Lattiq uses a thin wrapper over that plus a custom reconnection strategy (capped at maxReconnectAttempts: 10, exponential backoff) because the default tries forever and eats battery on mobile.</p> <p>The room is namespaced by document ID (doc-${docId}), so different documents are completely isolated. A user in one document cannot see or affect another.</p> <p>A flaky tube journey that would break a Google Docs session does nothing to a Lattiq session. The editor stays responsive the whole time. Changes save locally instantly. When the connection comes back, the sync happens in the background and the UI moves from offline to syncing to synced without interrupting the user.</p> <p>More importantly, the offline case is not a degraded mode. It is the canonical mode. The server is the optimisation layer, not the source of truth. That inversion is what makes the whole architecture feel different from a traditional collaborative editor, and it is what makes local-first editors trustworthy in a way that purely online ones never quite are.</p> <p>CRDTs are the thing that makes this possible. Everything else, IndexedDB, the Provider abstraction, the state machine, is just careful plumbing around the central guarantee: your edits converge with everyone else's, always, regardless of network conditions, and regardless of ordering.</p> <p>An editor that survives the Tube is the minimum standard.</p> <p>How I Fixed Retrograde Timing, Aspect Orbs, and Caching in My Astrology Engine</p> <p>Design engineer, AI product engineer and founder of Lunar Computing. I build products and write about the decisions underneath them.</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://hackernoon.com/building-a-local-first-collaborative-editor-with-yjs-lexical-and-indexeddb?source=rss" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9759"> <h2>#9759. WhatsApp OTP login with SMS fallback: 3 bugs that cost us sign-ups</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://media2.dev.to/dynamic/image/width=1200,height=627,fit=cover,gravity=auto,format=auto/https%3A%2F%2Fdev-to-uploads.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com%2Fuploads%2Farticles%2F7vu074rs8v26etietoxa.png" alt="WhatsApp OTP login with SMS fallback: 3 bugs that cost us sign-ups" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>Most of our users in India are delivery riders, guards, pickers and telecallers signing up on budget Android phones. SMS OTP was our biggest sign-up leak: messages arrived late or not at all, and every resend cost money. We moved the primary OTP channel to WhatsApp and kept SMS as a fallback. Here's how it works and the bugs we hit.</p> <p>Our OTP input had autocomplete="one-time-code". On Android, the keyboard then suggests the latest SMS code it has seen, often an old bank or delivery OTP. Combined with auto-submit at 6 digits, users "entered" a wrong code without typing anything. Fix: only set one-time-code when the channel is SMS; use off for WhatsApp.</p> <p>Each send overwrote the stored hash. WhatsApp messages sometimes arrive out of order, so users typed the first code after tapping resend and got "wrong OTP". Fix: keep the last two unexpired hashes alongside the new one and accept any of them until their own expiry.</p> <p>People type 9876543210 or 1234567890 to see what happens. That sends a real message to a stranger and leaves the user stuck. We now reject well-known placeholder numbers before sending, with a clear message.</p> <p>Wrong-OTP errors dropped right after these fixes, and WhatsApp delivery is noticeably faster than SMS for our users.</p> <p>If you're curious about the product, it's RollHire, a hiring app for local jobs in India.</p> <p>DEV Community — A space to discuss and keep up software development and manage your software career</p> <p>Built on Forem — the open source software that powers DEV and other inclusive communities.</p> <p>Made with love and Ruby on Rails. DEV Community © 2016 - 2026.</p> <p>We're a place where coders share, stay up-to-date and grow their careers.</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://dev.to/rollhire/whatsapp-otp-login-with-sms-fallback-3-bugs-that-cost-us-sign-ups-2aip" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9758"> <h2>#9758. Most Frequently Asked Questions About Affiliate Marketing</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p><p><span style="font-family: Frank Ruhl Libre;"></span></p><div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"><div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"><a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEjLCGYdIHSYPp0B6qIW9VwN-URfa73Wf2kKkpBANspBG-j_RryJDZcR8ud0YgtKoH_n450v_5Q_o8tX27XrZYmJ3bOTiWxUD4XjBdYcCMlDd_edn6ZnSFfxhx82zU_wtWgGDXB3H3awFvp6Dr0UayT_Hv7MV7-at2K1nY3N2L5nMc-MBSpOLL5e7VrIdw/s600/Most-Frequently-Asked-Questions-About-Email-Marketing-min.webp" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"><img alt="Most Frequently Asked Questions About Affiliate Marketing" border="0" height="360" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEjLCGYdIHSYPp0B6qIW9VwN-URfa73Wf2kKkpBANspBG-j_RryJDZcR8ud0YgtKoH_n450v_5Q_o8tX27XrZYmJ3bOTiWxUD4XjBdYcCMlDd_edn6ZnSFfxhx82zU_wtWgGDXB3H3awFvp6Dr0UayT_Hv7MV7-at2K1nY3N2L5nMc-MBSpOLL5e7VrIdw/w640-h360/Most-Frequently-Asked-Questions-About-Email-Marketing-min.webp" title="Most Frequently Asked Questions About Affiliate Marketing" width="640" /></a></div><br /><div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"><br /></div></div><p></p><p><span><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"></span></span></p><a name="more"></a><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">There are lots of questions floating around about how affiliate marketing works, what to do and what not to do when it comes to setting up a business. With so much uncertainty surrounding both personal and business aspects of affiliate marketing. In this post, we will answer the most frequently asked question about affiliate marketing</span><p></p><h3 style="text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">1. What is affiliate marketing?</span></h3><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"> Affiliate marketing is a way to make money by promoting the products and services of other people and companies. You don't need to create your product or service, just promote existing ones. That's why it's so easy to get started with affiliate marketing. You can even get started with no budget at all!</span></p><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><br /></span></p><h3 style="text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">2. What is an affiliate program?</span></h3><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"> An affiliate program is a package of information you create for your product, which is then made available to potential publishers. The program will typically include details about the product and its retail value, commission levels, and promotional materials. Many affiliate programs are managed via an affiliate network like ShareASale, which acts as a platform to connect publishers and advertisers, but it is also possible to offer your program directly.</span></p><h4 style="text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">3. What is an affiliate network and how do affiliate networks make money? </span></h4><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"> Affiliate networks connect publishers to advertisers.  Affiliate networks make money by charging fees to the merchants who advertise with them; these merchants are known as advertisers. The percentage of each sale that the advertiser pays is negotiated between the merchant and the affiliate network.</span></p><h4 style="text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">4. What's the difference between affiliate marketing and dropshipping?</span></h4><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"> Dropshipping is a method of selling that allows you to run an online store without having to stock products. You advertise the products as if you owned them, but when someone makes an order, you create a duplicate order with the distributor at a reduced price. The distributor takes care of the post and packaging on your behalf. As affiliate marketing is based on referrals and this type of drop shipping requires no investment in inventory when a customer buys through the affiliate link, no money exchanges hands.</span></p><h4 style="text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"> 5. Can affiliate marketing and performance marketing be considered the same thing?</span></h4><p><!--Ads Managed by AdSpyglass.com--> <span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"> Performance marketing is a method of marketing that pays for performance, like when a sale is made or an ad is clicked This can include methods like PPC (pay-per-click) or display advertising. Affiliate marketing is one form of performance marketing where commissions are paid out to affiliates on a performance basis when they click on their affiliate link and make a purchase or action.</span></p><h4 style="text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"> 6. Is it possible to promote affiliate offers on mobile devices?</span></h4><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"> Smartphones are essentially miniature computers, so publishers can display the same websites and offers that are available on a PC. But mobiles also offer specific tools not available on computers, and these can be used to good effect for publishers. Publishers can optimize their ads for mobile users by making them easy to access by this audience. Publishers can also make good use of text and instant messaging to promote their offers. As the mobile market is predicted to make up 80% of traffic in the future, publishers who do not promote on mobile devices are missing out on a big opportunity.</span></p><h4 style="text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">7. Where do I find qualified publishers?</span></h4><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"> The best way to find affiliate publishers is on reputable networks like ShareASale Cj(Commission Junction), Awin, and Impact radius. These networks have a strict application process and compliance checks, which means that all affiliates are trustworthy.</span></p><h4 style="text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">8. What is an affiliate disclosure statement?</span></h4><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"> An affiliate disclosure statement discloses to the reader that there may be affiliate links on a website, for which a commission may be paid to the publisher if visitors follow these links and make purchases.</span></p><h4 style="text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"> 9. Does social media activity play a significant role in affiliate marketing?</span></h4><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"> Publishers promote their programs through a variety of means, including blogs, websites, email marketing, and pay-per-click ads. Social media has a huge interactive audience, making this platform a good source of potential traffic.</span></p><h4 style="text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">10. What is a super affiliate?</span></h4><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"> A super affiliate is an affiliate partner who consistently drives a large majority of sales from any program they promote, compared to other affiliate partners involved in that program.  Affiliates make a lot of money from affiliate marketing Pat Flynn earned more than $50000 in 2013 from affiliate marketing.</span></p><h4 style="text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">11. How do we track publisher sales activity?</span></h4><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"> Publishers can be identified by their publisher ID, which is used in tracking cookies to determine which publishers generate sales. The activity is then viewed within a network's dashboard.</span></p><h4 style="text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"> 12. Could we set up an affiliate program in multiple countries?</span></h4><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"> Because the Internet is so widespread, affiliate programs can be promoted in any country. Affiliate strategies that are set internationally need to be tailored to the language of the targeted country.</span></p><h4 style="text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">13. How can affiliate marketing help my business?</span></h4><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Affiliate marketing can help you grow your business in the following ways:</span></p><p></p><ul style="text-align: left;"><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"> It allows you to save time and money on marketing, which frees you up to focus on other aspects of your business.</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"> You get access to friendly marketers who are eager to help you succeed. </span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">It also helps you to promote your products by sharing links and banners with a new audience.</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"> It offers high ROI(Return on investment) and is cost-effective.</span></li></ul><p></p><h4 style="text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"> 14. How do I find quality publishers?</span></h4><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"> One of the best ways to work with qualified affiliates is to hire an affiliate marketing agency that works with all the networks. Affiliates are carefully selected and go through a rigorous application process to be included in the network.</span></p><h4 style="text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">15. How Can we Promote Affiliate Links?</span></h4><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"> Affiliate marketing is generally associated with websites, but there are other ways to promote your affiliate links, including:</span></p><p></p><ul style="text-align: left;"><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">A website or blog</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Through email marketing and newsletter</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Social media, like Facebook, Instagram, or Twitter.</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"> Leave a comment on blogs or forums.</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Write an e-book or other digital product.</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Youtube</span></li></ul><p></p><h4 style="text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"> 16. Do you have to pay to sign up for an affiliate program?</span></h4><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"> To build your affiliate marketing business, you don't have to invest money in the beginning. You can sign up for free with any affiliate network and start promoting their brands right away.</span></p><h4 style="text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">17. What is a commission rate?</span></h4><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"> Commission rates are typically based on a percentage of the total sale and in some cases can also be a flat fee for each transaction. The rates are set by the merchant.</span></p><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Who manages your affiliate program?</span></p><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"> Some merchants run their affiliate programs internally, while others choose to contract out management to a network or an external agency.</span></p><h4 style="text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">18. What is a cookie?</span></h4><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"> Cookies are small pieces of data that work with web browsers to store information such as user preferences, login or registration data, and shopping cart contents. When someone clicks on your affiliate link, a cookie is placed on the user's computer or mobile device. That cookie is used to remember the link or ad that the visitor clicked on. Even if the user leaves your site and comes back a week later to make a purchase, you will still get credit for the sale and receive a commission it depends on the site cookies duration</span></p><h4 style="text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">19. How long do cookies last?</span></h4><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"> The merchant determines the duration of a cookie, also known as its “cookie life.” The most common length for an affiliate program is 30 days. If someone clicks on your affiliate link, you’ll be paid a commission if they purchase within 30 days of the click.</span></p><h3 style="text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Final Saying</span></h3><div><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Most new affiliates are eager to begin their affiliate marketing business. Unfortunately, there is a lot of bad information out there that can lead inexperienced affiliates astray. Hopefully, the answer to your question will provide clarity on how affiliate marketing works and the pitfalls you can avoid. Most importantly, keep in mind that success in affiliate marketing takes some time. Don't be discouraged if you're not immediately making sales or earning money. It takes most new affiliates months to make a full-time income.</span></div><p><br /></p></p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://techncruncher.blogspot.com/2022/06/most-frequently-asked-questions-about.html" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9757"> <h2>#9757.
