How Edge Firewalls Actually Fingerprint Python Scrapers in 2026 (JA4, HTTP/2 Frames & Client Hints)</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://media2.dev.to/dynamic/image/width=1200,height=627,fit=cover,gravity=auto,format=auto/https%3A%2F%2Fdev-to-uploads.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com%2Fuploads%2Farticles%2Fkptzlhpi0j1ok9uiayaz.png" alt="How Edge Firewalls Actually Fingerprint Python Scrapers in 2026 (JA4, HTTP/2 Frames & Client Hints)" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>Most web scraping literature is hopelessly stuck in 2018.</p> <p>The standard advice—installing requests, rotating an array of randomized desktop User-Agent strings, and running BeautifulSoup inside a naive loop—collapses the millisecond it hits modern Web Application Firewalls (Cloudflare, Akamai, DataDome, PerimeterX, AWS WAF).</p> <p>Modern edge security engines do not care about your Python code. They evaluate the mathematical coherence of your networking stack.</p> <p>In this architectural teardown, we will dissect the concentric layers of modern bot mitigation and explore how to build resilient, unblockable Python data engines without third-party subscriptions.</p> <p>Edge security systems evaluate incoming client sessions across three distinct protocol layers:</p> <p>When your Python crawler opens a TLS socket, it sends a ClientHello handshake message. Edge firewalls inspect the raw byte array of this handshake before sending a single byte of HTTP response.</p> <p>JA4 is a 36-character fingerprint comprising three hyphen-separated sections:</p> <p>$$\text{JA4} = \mathbf{t13d}_\mathbf{1508}_\mathbf{b2f4}\dots$$</p> <p>By default, Python's ssl module links against your system's OpenSSL dynamic library. OpenSSL advertises ciphers in a sequence that no consumer browser ever sends.</p> <p>When a request arrives claiming to be Chrome/131.0.0.0 on macOS, but its TLS handshake reveals an OpenSSL cipher suite order, the edge firewall assigns a Threat Score of 99/100 before parsing your headers.</p> <p>If your client passes TLS inspection, the edge evaluates your HTTP/2 connection framing.</p> <p>In HTTP/2, request metadata is transmitted as compressed binary headers (HPACK). Unlike HTTP/1.1 where headers are arbitrary strings, HTTP/2 specifies four pseudo-headers:</p> <p>The legacy User-Agent string is formally deprecated. Modern Chromium browsers communicate client capabilities via structured Client Hints:</p> <p>To build a reliable crawler, your code must enforce Header Coherence:</p> <p>If you are designing high-throughput data pipelines or enterprise crawlers, explore our full production ecosystem:</p> <p>Happy building, and keep your data pipelines unblockable!</p> <p>DEV Community — A space to discuss and keep up software development and manage your software career</p> <p>Built on Forem — the open source software that powers DEV and other inclusive communities.</p> <p>Made with love and Ruby on Rails. DEV Community © 2016 - 2026.</p> <p>We're a place where coders share, stay up-to-date and grow their careers.</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://dev.to/mzulfaas/how-edge-firewalls-actually-fingerprint-python-scrapers-in-2026-ja4-http2-frames-client-hints-4nf5" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9754"> <h2>#9754. Salus</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p><p> Discover benefits and public support in the Czech Republic </p> <p> <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/products/salus?utm_campaign=producthunt-atom-posts-feed&utm_medium=rss-feed&utm_source=producthunt-atom-posts-feed">Discussion</a> | <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/r/p/1319569?app_id=339">Link</a> </p></p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/products/salus" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9753"> <h2>#9753. Dozy</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p><p> Turns your sleep data into one thing to do today </p> <p> <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/products/dozy?utm_campaign=producthunt-atom-posts-feed&utm_medium=rss-feed&utm_source=producthunt-atom-posts-feed">Discussion</a> | <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/r/p/1323490?app_id=339">Link</a> </p></p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/products/dozy" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9752"> <h2>#9752. Comparing Qini, IPW, and Doubly Robust Metrics for Uplift Modeling</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://hackernoon.imgix.net/images/3ay66sIqG8Noq9fK97KXwmfcMTd2-st03b8q.png" alt="Comparing Qini, IPW, and Doubly Robust Metrics for Uplift Modeling" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>Staff Data Scientist at Careem. Writing about causal inference, experimentation, and practical AI—from model assumptions to real decisions.</p> <p>Staff Data Scientist at Careem. Writing about causal inference, experimentation, and practical AI—from model assumptions to real decisions.</p> <p>Staff Data Scientist at Careem. Writing about causal inference, experimentation, and practical AI—from model assumptions to real decisions.</p> <p>Why causal estimation needs causal evaluation, and how Inverse Propensity Weighting and Doubly Robust scores change model comparisons</p> <p>What if your uplift metric ranked an imperfect model above the true treatment-effect ranking? In a simulation where we know the answer, Qini can do exactly that, and following its recommendation means choosing a ranking with lower true causal gain.</p> <p>Let’s start with the classical uplift problem. Suppose a company needs to decide which customers of theirs to send marketing messages to. The best ranking of customers would be based on the expected benefit from sending them a marketing message, which depends on the value of the action we try to nudge them to and the shift in the probability of performing this action due to the receiving the communication. Of course, the company doesn’t know these probabilities, so it uses an imperfect ranking based on their estimates.</p> <p>Let’s take a hypothetical situation in which we know the real probabilities, that means we know the real perfect ranking of the customers in terms of the efficiency of communication. Suppose we decided to compare it with the imperfect ranking based on our estimates of these probabilities. Funny thing — it occurs that the Qini metric (which is often used for uplift measurement and will be described further) will assign better score to the imperfect ranking. How could it be?</p> <p>Throughout this article, Qini and IPW are calibrated to match DR at one reference: the true-CATE ranking in the higher-selectivity, seed-42 holdout. The constants stay fixed for all learners, bootstrap resamples, assignment policies and tuning results. This aligns the reference scores, but does not adjust for confounding or change the ordering of models within a metric. In this example, calibrated Qini still favors Linear DR over the true-CATE ranking, whereas known causal gain favors true CATE. The calibration formula is given below.</p> <p>The reason is that it’s often not enough to use a causal model that accounts for the confounding. If we have the treatment assignment dependent on the customer characteristics, we also need to adjust the metric to evaluate this causal model, as the Qini metric still can contain the selection bias.</p> <p>In this article, we will go through the whole evolution of our attempts to measure the causal effect — from the uplift bars, through the Qini metric towards the IPW and doubly robust scores to evaluate the models. We will use six common learners from S learner to DML learner, and will see how we can assess their estimates depending on different degrees of confounding.</p> <p>For a given treatment T (a marketing message) and an outcome Y (a customer’s actual purchase) a customer’s Conditional Average</p> <p>CATE can be perceived as the average treatment effect (ATE) for a given customer with profile x. It can be used for customer targeting since high CATE shows that the the effect of the treatment on this customer is higher. Just to highlight — it doesn’t mean the customer with high CATE has the highest outcome or the probability of making some action. It means that if contacted, the customer has the highest uplift in this outcome or probability compared to the situation when the customer isn’t contacted.</p> <p>Usually, companies have limited budgets for their marketing activities, so the ranking is instrumental to understand how to optimally distribute the budget for these activities.</p> <p>In this article, we will compare the 6 models based on the synthetic data using different metrics. In our case we know the true treatment effect, which is usually not the case. This approach allows us to make a comparison and study the uplift metrics in detail.</p> <p>It represents the difference in treatment probability, depending on the user profile. Irrespective of the metric and evaluation method and the model — we need some number of conditions to be satisfied so that our causal estimator works: consistency, no relevant interference, no unmeasured confounding and overlap.</p> <p>We simulate 1 million individual synthetic customers for which we have several characteristics: age, income, past spending over time, time since last contact with the customer. We simulate a factual communication policy that depends on the two dimensions: age and last contact activity,</p> <p>where a is the intercept for calibration, and Z is the standardized product of age and last contact activity. We have provided the executable code for the outcome in the companion.</p> <p>To simulate this type of data, the following parameters are fixed for the communication policy: the probability is to be between 0.1 and 0.9, with 50% treated on average. The inactivity and age of the customer are used to predict the probability of communication with the customer.</p> <p>The purchase probability is also based on a logistic function and dependent on customer characteristics. Moreover, the treatment effect itself is nonuniform and impacts different customers in a different way.</p> <p>Below in the code you may see the simulation algorithm:</p> <p>For every profile we calculate p₁(x), p₀(x) and TrueCATE=p₁(x)−p₀(x). As the treatment groups in the simulation are almost of equal size the mean of the true-CATE values for the treated customers is approximately +0.191 and for the controls −0.003. The observed purchase-rate difference is 0.119. The ATE for this simulation is 0.094 (all numbers are rounded to 3 FP digits).</p> <p>Below are the graphs which allow us to have a high-level understanding of the data we have generated:</p> <p>We trained on 700k customers and then evaluated on the 300k held-out customers using seed 42 for this example. Each of the S, T, X, DA, DR, DML estimators was implemented using both linear and “boosted” base models. Note that all of the estimators above (S,T,X,DA,DR,DML) have lengthy derivations and are material for another article. Here I will just provide the high-level intuition of the algorithms.</p> <p>The models used for this article are the EconML implementations (the S- and T-learners as well as the DA-, DR-, and DML-learners with a linear and XGBoost base model).</p> <p>Our starting point will be an S-learner as the simplest and the most intuitive model. Its holdout MSE against the true CATE is 0.0006, with correlation 0.9964. That tells us its effect estimates are quite accurate in this simulation. But in reality we don’t know the true effect, so we need another way to assess targeting.</p> <p>The most obvious way to do this is an uplift barplot. We sort customers by the CATE, divide them into buckets and compare treatment and control outcomes for the buckets.</p> <p>The graphs look useful: the right-hand buckets have larger observed differences than the left-hand ones. However, those differences are not quite the true effects. Grouping by predicted CATE does not necessarily make the treatment and control customers comparable inside each bucket — they can be very different in their characteristics.</p> <p>The plot helps us inspect a model, but we should not interpret its bar differences as causal effects or use only them to decide who should receive treatment.</p> <p>Quite often we just need one number, which allows us to compare different estimators. Something similar to the ROC AUC score we sometimes use to assess classification models. That’s where the Qini AUC comes into play.</p> <p>Instead of having a bar plot that compares uplift for a number of different buckets of customers, look at the single customer with the highest predicted value of treatment. Then add the next customer with the highest predicted value, then the next customer, and so on. For each customer added in the group we calculate the total positive outcomes for the treatment and control.</p> <p>Rₜ(k) and R꜀(k) denote the positive-outcome totals for the treatment group and the control group, respectively, for the top k customers. Let Nₜ (k) and N꜀ (k) denote the arm sizes for the treatment group and the control group.</p> <p>Let p̂=Nₜ(N)/N be the observed treatment share in the evaluation sample. First, define q(f)=Q(k)/(Np̂), where f=k/N, and let A_Q be its area above the line connecting the start and end points:</p> <p>Zero is the reference area for random targeting; finite-sample scores can fluctuate around it. The normalization by N and horizontal fraction f=k/N are already included above, so we do not divide this area by N² again. Dividing by the treatment share supplies the causal-gain unit convention, but does not remove selection bias.</p> <p>For the additional calibration, let r₀ denote the true-CATE ranking in the higher-selectivity, seed-42 holdout. We use DR as the reference score and calculate the fixed divisors:</p> <p>All displayed evaluation areas and differences then use:</p> <p>All three reference scores are therefore start as 0.0826. The curve below is also divided by c_Q, so its area matches the tables. This is an oracle-assisted calibration for this simulation: it requires knowing the true-CATE ranking and does not establish that the scores estimate the same quantity accurately. They are calibrated only for comparability purposes. The calibration preserves each evaluator’s model ordering. We freeze these constants everywhere, including within bootstrap resamples.</p> <p>Numbers are rounded for display. Differences and confidence intervals are calculated before rounding, so equal displayed scores need not be identical.</p> <p>Here is the S-learner’s Qini curve for the illustration:</p> <p>The main problem is that the Qini metric in its evaluation still uses the observed treatments and outcome variables. Remember that the customers were selected for treatment based on their characteristics; thus, the treatment/control differences still contain selection bias.</p> <p>A causal learner estimates the treatment effect. If done correctly, it is potentially unconfounded. But the metric is still confounded, as it is observational! We’ve seen it already at the graph with the uplift bars — the difference was not matching the true effect.</p> <p>This mismatch might be an insignificant calculation artifact if it wasn’t for its potential effect on qualitative conclusions based on the analysis. In our example, when we compare the models, the Linear DR learner gives us better metrics than the “oracle” model, which knows the true CATE. This is indicative of a large problem. Now we know we can’t trust Qini, because it can choose a wrong estimator for us.</p> <p>Therefore, we now understand that we need to improve not just a learner, but the evaluation as well. The ideal situation of course — randomized treatment assignment. But when we have only biased observational data — we can use Inverse-Propensity Weighting (IPW) or Doubly Robust (DR) score which we discuss below.</p> <p>Inverse-propensity weighting gives each observed outcome a weight based on how likely its assignment was:</p> <p>Doubly robust scoring also uses the outcome prediction and the residual, but weights the residual by the inverse propensity score of the customer.</p> <p>In the formulas above, T means the treatment flag, Y — the outcome variable. ê(X_i) — the propensity model (probability of being treated), μ̂₀(X_i) and μ̂₁(X_i) — the models of the outome prediction under treatment and control.</p> <p>Usually, the DR-learner uses the same pseudo-outcome as you see above to fit effects, but here we are not looking for it — we are evaluating a trained ranking. The ranking can come from any model — not just the DR-learner.</p> <p>Next step — we sort customers by the model-ranked scores, summing up the corresponding scores:</p> <p>These are the uncalibrated IPW and DR gain curves. IPW and DR adjust for confounding under their respective assumptions. Under randomized assignment, treatment-share-normalized Qini targets the same causal-gain convention. For display throughout this article, we additionally divide the IPW curve and area by the fixed reference divisor c_IPW; DR stays unchanged. Calibration is separate from the causal adjustment.</p> <p>For the adjusted methods, we estimate a propensity model and two outcome models separately from the main ranking model. They are called the nuisance models. They are estimated using the observable variables X, T, and Y. For the nuisance models, we use three-fold crossfitting, which guarantees that for both predictions the customer was excluded from the training sample for the models. All rankings use the same evaluation scores.</p> <p>Running the following Python code in the companion directory trains the S-learner and, in addition, fits separate evaluation models.</p> <p>The errors in the evaluation of different estimators are close to each other, so we better look at the error of the score of each ranking with respect to the causal gain of that ranking, which is known from the data generation process (thanks to our synthetic dataset!).</p> <p>After calibration, Qini’s residual errors across the six boosted rankings range from +0.0002 to +0.0008. Calibrated IPW errors range from +0.0001 to +0.0002, and DR errors from +0.0001 to +0.0002. Qini favors the wrong ranking in the Linear-DR comparison below.</p> <p>The disagreement matters for model choice, too:</p> <p>The “true gain” is the area above the endpoint diagonal of the cumulative true-CATE curve for each ranking. IPW and DR produce scores close to these known gains and favor the true-CATE ranking over Linear DR. They do not reproduce every small ordering difference among the boosted learners. Calibrated Qini still favors Linear DR over the true-CATE ranking.</p> <p>When you use these methods — keep in mind that IPW still requires a correct propensity model, and DR still requires a correct propensity OR both outcome models. Both scorers require consistency, no unmeasured confounding and overlap. Estimated models and finite samples leave residual error, so these approaches are not automatically unbiased scores for every dataset. So, you use it, but be careful as always.</p> <p>We have only compared point estimates for the different models so far. It might be interesting to see how large the differences are between the estimates for another random set of evaluation customers (i.e. different realization of the holdout sample of 300k customers with their respective multiplicities). In other words — are these differences statistically significant and consistent?</p> <p>In order to investigate this we conducted 1,000 paired bootstrap resamples of the 300,000 customers in the holdout data set. For each of the resampled evaluation data sets, we computed the statistics of interest for all models and all evaluation methods. The resulting values’ 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles are provided in brackets below.</p> <p>These are the conditional 95% percentile intervals. Note that we hold the trained models and nuisance functions fixed and resampling only the evaluation part. This means we don’t guarantee the 95% coverage for the full procedure bootstrap. The experiment is repeated later with 3 different seeds to ensure the conclusions are robust.</p> <p>Note that overlying intervals do not directly answer questions of whether one model is better than another. More relevant are the intervals for the paired differences between the two models under consideration (how much one model is better than another). Below we compared each of the models with the oracle truth.</p> <p>Choosing a CATE estimator is a broader topic that deserves a separate article. For this example, I would choose the XGBoost S-learner as a simple starting point. It has the simplest estimation structure among the six learners considered: one outcome model, with treatment included as an input feature. The DML estimator has the highest DR-gain point estimate among the six boosted learners, but its advantage over S is small: the paired S-minus-DML difference is -0.00006, with a conditional 95% interval which includes zero. That does not prove equivalence and this is not the claim that S learner is always the best. But if the difference in the 5th digit is not critical for your application, I would choose the S-learner for this specific case. Simplicity wins.</p> <p>The comparison of S with T has a positive DR-area difference of +0.0002 with a Conditional 95% Interval of [+0.00003, +0.0003]. So, within these models and this fixed set of nuisance fits, S has a statistically significant DR-area difference compared with T. The paired intervals for the comparisons with X, DA, DR, and DML all include zero, so there is no evidence of a consistently higher DR area for S.</p> <p>We don’t use Qini here anymore, because we’ve seen before that its confoundedness affects its conclusions even on a qualitative scale. Even increasing bootstrap sample for the Qini won’t make it unbiased, so we can stop using it.</p> <p>We have so far followed one data generation to model comparison example. Let’s now slightly change the assignment policy and check if the results are stable under different assignments.</p> <p>We will replace 2.5 in the propensity rule by 0.5 and by 1, affecting the selection bias and we will call it “low” and “middle” selectivity. The population treatment share will still be 50% as we have calibrated our assignment in this way. We will also refit all the learners for 3 different seeds for robustness.</p> <p>For this figure, we rank customers directly by their known true CATE. No S, T or other learner supplies the ranking. We hold the customer profiles and this perfect ordering fixed across assignment policies within each seed, then change which customers receive treatment and which outcomes we observe. The question is whether each evaluator can accurately score the same ranking as assignment becomes more selective.</p> <p>All three evaluators’ point estimates will coincide in the “higher” selection policy by construction because of the calibration we’ve done for comparability. The valibration is made based on the true CATE and we are considering the true CATE ranking in this case. What is interesting is how the rankers behave in case of the changes in the assignment policy.</p> <p>We see that the DR and IPW behave quite stable, and the Qini is not stable at all and changing a lot depending on the assignment policy. This is one more evidence of how it can be influenced by different levels of selection bias.</p> <p>All three runs of increased selectivity show the same reversal between Linear DR and true CATE as was seen in the single run of increased selectivity. The expected-count diagnostic is also well-behaved. This constitutes more empirical evidence for the phenomenon than a single lucky or unlucky run. (Of course, three runs do not guarantee to cover the variability in all possible datasets.)</p> <p>What about hyperparameter tuning? The evaluator also affects which hyperparameters do we select! We gave each of the six boosted learners 15 configurations, including its default. The original 700,000 training customers were split into 500,000 for fitting candidates and 200,000 for validation. Then we selected each learner’s configuration using cross-fitted DR gain on that validation sample, without using true CATE.</p> <p>Then we have frozen the selected hyperparameters before generating a fresh 300,000-customer test sample from the ”high” selectivity policy. Both default and selected models were refitted on the same original 700,000 training customers, then evaluated on these new test customers with shared cross-fitted evaluation models. The earlier article holdout was not used in this tuning comparison. So, do not attribute differences from earlier tables to tuning alone. Below you will see the illustrated effect of the tuning on the three metrics considered before and on the RMSE metric which is calculated relative to the true CATE which we know as we have generated our dataset (it’s omitted from other sections, because in reality we never know the true CATE).</p> <p>The direction of the effect from our tuning is not clear for S, X, DA, DR, DML learners as the intervals include zero, which corresponds to no change in the values. But for T-learner the paired intervals all favor tuning which also improves the CATE RMSE from 0.0328 to 0.0237. S-learner has the most extreme behavior where the DR point estimate decreased, and the CATE RMSE increased from 0.0243 to 0.0316 on the fresh test sample. So our tuning in case of the S-learner was not very fruitful.</p> <p>To be clear, it’s still hard to compare the tuning of such different models, as the number of potential hyperparameter changes is different for a simple S-learner and for the DML. But the idea of this section is to show that the hyperparameter runing doesn’t change the ranking effect of confounded metric (Qini) we’ve shown before.</p> <p>In conclusion, let’s try to formulate — what should we do when comparing the uplift models quality? First evaluate the assignment to treatment in your experiment. If the assignment to treatment is not random (as in most cases) then a familiar uplift plot or Qini curve don’t work anymore. Use both an evaluation design and the estimator which assumptions still hold (don’t require random assignment).</p> <p>Using IPW and a DR evaluator of causal gain on the the data gave scores close to the known causal gain and kept the estimators ranking correct. I would opt in for the DR evaluation, well, because it’s Doubly Robust, so it’s still valid even if one of its assumptions failed.</p> <p>Ultimately, for your marketing campaign (or any other application of the uplift model) look at what’s important for your case: the budget, cost and incremental value for a given budget. Area under the curve is interesting but not what you ar optimizing for as the business objective.</p> <p>The separate evaluation companion contains evaluation.ipynb, the shared model and metric implementation, all numerical tables, paired bootstrap draws, figures and the tuning protocol. Its default notebook run analyzes the completed experiments and independently checks IPW/DR formulas from stored observed rows and nuisance predictions.</p> <p>python reproduce.py --output regenerated recreates all baseline fits, evaluator fits, diagnostics, resamples, tuning and figures in a new directory. The single code example above is supplied as article_example.py. The README distinguishes these full fitting steps from quick notebook analysis. Three-policy seed ranges and fixed-fit bootstrap intervals retain their separate meanings.</p> <p>[1] PyWhy, EconML Meta-Learners, version 0.16.0 documentation.</p> <p>[2] E. H. Kennedy, Towards optimal doubly robust estimation of heterogeneous causal effects (2020; revised 2023), arXiv.</p> <p>[3] scikit-uplift contributors, Metric implementation, version 0.5.1 documentation.</p> <p>[4] grf contributors, Assessing heterogeneity with RATE, documentation. Our own conditional row-bootstrap procedure is used in this article instead of grf’s implementation of RATE for causal heterogeneity inference.</p> <p>Staff Data Scientist at Careem. src="https://www.spring.org.uk/images/pills-6-1.jpg" alt="5 Types Of Brain-Affecting Drugs Still Prescribed Despite Safety Warnings" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>Five drug groups carry warnings for older adults, yet prescribing remains highest among those with dementia.</p> <p>Five drug groups carry warnings for older adults, yet prescribing remains highest among those with dementia.</p> <p>One in four older Americans with dementia is prescribed potentially inappropriate medicines that affect the brain and nervous system.</p> <p>These drugs can increase the risk of confusion, falls and hospitalisation, particularly in people whose thinking and memory are already impaired.</p> <p>Despite decades of warnings, people with cognitive impairment were more likely to receive these prescriptions than those with normal cognition.</p> <p>The research examined five categories of medication flagged by prescribing guidelines for older adults:</p> <p>Only antidepressants with strong anticholinergic properties were included in this category.</p> <p>Anticholinergic medicines block acetylcholine, a chemical messenger involved in memory, learning and concentration.</p> <p>Blocking its action can cause confusion and other unwanted effects, especially in older adults.</p> <p>Benzodiazepines, which may be prescribed for anxiety or sleep problems, can cause excessive drowsiness and increase the risk of falls.</p> <p>Some medicines also take longer to leave the body as people age, allowing their effects to persist or accumulate.</p> <p>The researchers analysed survey information linked to medical insurance records from almost 4,900 Americans aged 65 and over.</p> <p>They examined prescribing over nine years, counting prescriptions for at least four weeks’ supply.</p> <p>Around 17 percent of people with normal cognition received at least one potentially inappropriate prescription, compared with almost 22 percent of those with cognitive impairment without dementia.</p> <p>Among people with dementia, the proportion reached 25 percent.</p> <p>Across the older adults studied, prescribing fell from around 20 percent at the beginning of the study period to 16 percent at the end.</p> <p>Much of the decline reflected fewer prescriptions for benzodiazepines and Z-drug sleeping medicines.</p> <p>However, prescribing rates for the other three drug groups did not change significantly.</p> <p>By the final year, more than two-thirds of people receiving these potentially inappropriate prescriptions lacked a documented clinical reason for at least one of them.</p> <p>A potentially inappropriate medicine can still be justified when its expected benefits outweigh its risks.</p> <p>The practical question is whether each prescription remains suitable for the person taking it.</p> <p>Dr Annie Yang, the study’s first author, emphasised the importance of patients and carers reviewing these medicines with their physicians:</p> <p>“While CNS-active prescriptions may be appropriate in some cases, it is important for older patients or their caregivers to work closely with their physicians to ensure that these medications are appropriate to their cases.</p> <p>When inappropriate, patients and their care teams should consider alternative treatments and consider whether it might be safe to taper or stop the medication.”</p> <p>The study was published in JAMA (Yang et al., 2026).</p> <p>Psychologist, Jeremy Dean, PhD is the founder and author of PsyBlog. He holds a doctorate in psychology from University College London and two other advanced degrees in psychology. He has been writing about scientific research on PsyBlog since 2004. Copilot</span></h3><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Copilot is a suite of tools that help eCommerce businesses maintain real-time communication with customers around the clock at every stage of the funnel. Promote products, recover shopping carts and send updates or reminders directly through Messenger.</span></p><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><b>Key features: </b></span></p><p></p><ul style="text-align: left;"><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Integrate Facebook Messenger directly with your website, including chat history and recent interactions for a fluid customer service experience </span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Run drip messenger campaigns to keep customers engaged with your brand</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Send abandoned carts, out-of-stock, restock, preorder, order status, and shipment notifications to contacts </span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Send branded images, promotional content, or coupon codes to those who opt in</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Collect post-purchase feedback, reviews, and customer insight</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Demonstrate social proof on your website with a widget, or push automatic Facebook posts sharing recent purchases</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Display a promotional banner on your website to capture contacts instantly</span></li></ul><div><b style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Also Read: <a href="https://www.crunchhype.com/2022/11/top-10-ai-content-generator-writer.html" target="_blank">Top 10 AI Content Generator & Writer Tools in 2022</a></b></div><p></p><h3 style="text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">10. Yotpo</span></h3><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Yotpo’s deep learning technology evaluates your customers’ product reviews to help you make better business decisions. It identifies key topics that customers mention related to your products—and their feelings toward them. The AI engine extracts relevant reviews from past buyers and presents them in smart displays to convert new shoppers. Yotpo also saves you time moderating reviews. The AI-powered moderation tool automatically assigns a score to each review and flags reviews with negative sentiment so you can focus on quality control instead of manually reviewing every post.</span></p><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><b>Key features:</b></span></p><p></p><ul style="text-align: left;"><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Makes it easy for shoppers to filter reviews and find the exact information they’re looking for</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Analyzes customer feedback and sentiments to help you improve your products</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Integrates with most leading eCommerce platforms, including BigCommerce, Magento, and Shopify.</span></li></ul><p></p><h3 style="text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">11. Albert AI</span></h3><p>  <span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Albert is a self-learning software that automates the creation of marketing campaigns for your brand. It analyzes vast amounts of data to run optimized campaigns autonomously, allowing you to feed in your own creative content and target markets, and then use data from its database to determine key characteristics of a serious buyer. Albert identifies potential customers that match those traits, and runs trial campaigns on a small group of customers—with results refined by Albert himself—before launching it on a larger scale.</span></p><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">  Albert plugs into your existing marketing technology stack, so you still have access to your accounts, ads, search, social media, and more. Albert maps tracking and attribution to your source of truth so you can determine which channels are driving your business.</span></p><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><b>Key features:</b></span></p><p></p><ul style="text-align: left;"><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Breaks down large amounts of data to help you customize campaigns</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Plugs into your marketing technology stack and can be used across diverse media outlets, including email, content, paid media, and mobile</span></li></ul><div><br /></div> <div id="atContainer-876e841c5466fc380c36e872fae9a8bb"></div> <h3 style="text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Final Saying</span></h3><p></p><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"></span></p><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">There are many tools and companies out there that offer AI tools, but this is a small list of resources that we have found to be helpful. If you have any other suggestions, feel free to share them in the comments below this article. As marketing evolves at such a rapid pace, new marketing strategies will be invented that we haven't even dreamed of yet. But for now, this list should give you a good starting point on your way to implementing AI into your marketing mix.</span></p><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><b><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Note: This article contains affiliate links, meaning we make a small commission if you buy any premium plan from our link.</span></b></span></p><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><br /></span></p></p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://techncruncher.blogspot.com/2022/07/top-10-ai-marketing-tools-you-should-use.html" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9747"> <h2>#9747. margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/sites/default/files/2025-05/Gluten-Free-Brownies-6.jpg" alt="13 gluten-free dessert recipes : There's something for everyone." style="max-width:100%; color: #333;"> <p>The lack of flour in this recipe creates a velvety, fudgy cake that also happens to be gluten-free. Swooshed with a glossy chocolate ganache on top, this cake is a chocolate lover’s dream.</p> <p>To make this recipe, you’ll need: Callebaut Semisweet Chocolate Chips</p> <p>To make this classic fall dessert gluten-free, you just need to use gluten-free flour in both the pie crust and as a thickener. It can be difficult to achieve a flaky crust without conventional flour, but we’ve dialed in the perfect ratio of gluten-free flour to butter. Everything else you know and love about the dessert stays the same: a buttery crust and sweet, spiced apples.</p> <p>To make this recipe, you’ll need: Gluten-Free Measure for Measure Flour</p> <p>To make this recipe, you’ll need: Almond Extract</p> <p>This crustless cheesecake is much more than the sum of its parts. Made with just cream cheese, sugar, salt, eggs, and heavy cream, it rewards you with a blistered, blackened exterior and a meltingly smooth interior. If you want to give it an autumnal spin, you can also make this pumpkin version.</p> <p>Get the recipe: Basque Cheesecake (Tarta de Queso)</p> <p>To make this recipe, you’ll need: Half-Sheet Parchment Paper</p> <p>To make this recipe, you’ll need: Triple Cocoa Blend</p> <p>If you're craving a classic treat or just need a reliable, easy dessert, this single-layer vanilla cake has you covered. It’s everything a weeknight bake should be: easy, quick, irresistibly moist, and full of flavor. Dress it up with chocolate ganache, macerated berries, or just a sprinkle of confectioners’ sugar.</p> <p>Get the recipe: Gluten-Free Vanilla Cake Pan Cake</p> <p>To make this recipe, you’ll need: Vanilla Extract</p> <p>Cheesecake may have a reputation for being fussy, but this recipe keeps things refreshingly simple. No springform pan, no water bath — just four basic ingredients for the filling: cream cheese, sugar, eggs, and vanilla. To make it gluten-free, just swap in gluten-free graham crackers for the press-in crust.</p> <p>To make this recipe, you’ll need: Pie Pan</p> <p>To make this recipe, you’ll need: Triple Cocoa Blend</p> <p>The magic of this buttery, moist cake is two-fold: The almond flour-based batter is naturally gluten-free, and it comes together in just 10 minutes. As the cake bakes, the fresh berry topping sinks into the velvety, smooth crumb. No additional décor needed: The jewel-toned berries are all you need.</p> <p>To make this recipe, you’ll need: Almond Flour</p> <p>This golden Bundt cake is extra-moist and nicely tangy due to its fresh lemon juice glaze, while gluten-free flour ensures a soft, tender crumb.</p> <p>Get the recipe: Gluten-Free Lemon Bliss Cake</p> <p>To make this recipe, you’ll need: Almond Flour</p> <p>To make this recipe, you’ll need: Chocolate Chips</p> <p>This cake is clearly a showstopper with its towering layers of tender cake, rich chocolate mousse, and fresh raspberries. This project bake will require some additional effort, but it’s well worth it for a special occasion.</p> <p>Get the recipe: Gluten-Free Chocolate Mousse Cake with Raspberries</p> <p>To make this recipe, you’ll need: Round Cake Pan</p> <p>Brownies are the perfect candidate to go gluten-free. Since gluten usually adds chewiness and structure to baked goods, these brownies are even richer and fudgier without it.</p> <p>To make this recipe, you’ll need: Gluten-Free All-Purpose Flour</p> <p>Cover photo (Gluten-Free Brownies) and food styling by Liz Neily.</p> <p>Need to stock up on gluten-free baking ingredients? Check out our full collection of gluten-free flours, mixes, and dessert cups.</p> <p>Transform your favorite bread loaf into shareable rolls.</p> <p>Top tips from the Things Bakers Know podcast.</p> <p>See our complete collection of Recipes posts.</p> <p>Skip the store-bought stuff and bake gluten-free bread at home instead.</p> <p>For the fudgiest brownies, ditch the flour</p> <p>Everything you need to know to start making gluten-free sourdough.</p> <p>Gluten-free starter is possible! color: #333;"> <p><table align="center" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" class="tr-caption-container" style="margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;"><tbody><tr><td style="text-align: center;"><a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEi8kcwgpveuAhQh6a74WIog7WmHGeIKPnsnbKEEFH6nIormpDBAefwpxDtXtltjW0FJ8UIoPG1oNNnw_MaXBH9pGFCePKsXs5UrWVopiEdCecN2ngJoUpzTZ_EZXi9k54pI0-pIYLeETvBJspPijCHXGLz9owRA6Ahjdvtz00lun1dSfdXNWbfIcyy9Lg/s1920/20220910_132213_0000.webp" style="margin-left: auto; If you're not interested, I'll share some of the best CJ affiliate programs and alternatives. By the end of this post, I will also answer some of the FAQs on the platform and give my quick CJ review. </span></div><div><span style="font-family: Quicksand;"><br /></span></div><div><span style="font-family: Quicksand;">Sounds Good So let’s start</span></div><h3 style="text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Quicksand;">What is CJ Affiliate?</span></h3><div><span style="font-family: Quicksand;">Commission Junction is an online advertising company that offers affiliate programs for various retailers. Since 1998, it has been known as one of the oldest and most popular affiliate networks. </span></div><div><span style="font-family: Quicksand;"><br /></span></div><div><span style="font-family: Quicksand;"> Commission Junction has consistently ranked among the top 10 affiliate networks </span></div><div><span style="font-family: Quicksand;"><br /></span></div> <div id="atContainer-2060cf2f0491455d459b6b7a0ee275f3"></div><div><span style="font-family: Quicksand;">With in-depth data analysis and an unmatched understanding of clients needs, CJ has established itself as a leader in performance marketing.</span></div><div><span style="font-family: Quicksand;"><br /></span></div><h4 style="text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Quicksand;">For Advertiser:</span></h4><div><span style="font-family: Quicksand;">CJ provides advertisers with a variety of tracking, management, and payment options. As an affiliate network, CJ can help you launch multiple affiliate programs from a centralized network. </span></div><div><span style="font-family: Quicksand;"> CJ's experienced team of account managers is available to help at every step—from program set-up to optimization.</span></div><div><span style="font-family: Quicksand;"><br /></span></div><h4 style="text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Quicksand;">For Publishers: </span></h4><div><span style="font-family: Quicksand;">CJ offers a  variety of well-paying affiliate programs. You can find affiliate programs in almost every niche at CJ. With CJ, you can also find promotional tools such as banners and product feeds, which help you promote your website. </span></div><div><span style="font-family: Quicksand;"><br /></span></div><div><span style="font-family: Quicksand;"> The reporting tools are unparalleled and provide granular data that can assist you in fine-tuning your campaigns for maximum results.</span></div><div><span style="font-family: Quicksand;"><br /></span></div><h4 style="text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Quicksand;">Requirements </span></h4><div><span style="font-family: Quicksand;"><br /></span></div><div><span style="font-family: Quicksand;">First things first, CJ is free to join! This fall, reach for this unlikely apple ingredient : Apple cider vinegar is a baker’s secret weapon.</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/sites/default/files/2025-07/Tarte-Tartin_2025_Lifestyle_ALT_H_1236.jpg" alt="This fall, reach for this unlikely apple ingredient : Apple cider vinegar is a baker’s secret weapon." style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>As fall baking season settles in, you're probably reaching for apples — and the many flavor-packed ingredients they produce. Applesauce cooks down into tangy apple butter to be cradled in a flaky galette, while a drop of boiled cider can deliver supercharged apple flavor to crumb cake. But the baking ingredient you may be overlooking may be something you associate more with salad dressings and wellness tonics: apple cider vinegar.</p> <p>This tangy, apple-y vinegar is a secret ingredient in some of our favorite fall recipes, including cookbook author Claire Saffitz’s Cinnamon-and-Sugar Apple Pie. While lemon juice is the standard acid used in most fruit pie fillings, Claire opts for apple cider vinegar here to complement the filling’s flavors. “It helps as a flavor enhancer, and I also like that it’s apple cider in an apple pie. It’s a nice symmetry,” she mentions.</p> <p>Similarly, apple cider vinegar is used in the cooking liquid alongside sugar and butter to caramelize apples in a Classic Apple Tarte Tatin. The benefit is twofold: Vinegar’s acidity helps cut the sweetness of the caramel, and it prevents the apples from getting too mushy, instead maintaining their fork-tender texture.</p> <p>Pastry chef and cookbook author Natasha Pickowicz often leans into the jolt vinegar can add, including adding a few drops to her cake soaks for an additional layer of flavor. “Cake soaks should have a balance of tart, sweet, and savory notes — just like vinaigrette for your favorite salad,” she writes in her cookbook More Than Cake. It can add intrigue to layered cakes like this Golden Spice Cake or Pumpkin Layer Cake. In her cookbook, she also calls for a glaze spiked with apple cider vinegar to brush onto an apple tart after baking. It’s the finishing touch “to further emphasize the tart’s resolute apple-ness,” she writes.</p> <p>Apple cider vinegar doesn’t need to be limited to only apple desserts, either. In our Old-Fashioned Pecan Pie, we call for apple cider vinegar as a foil to the brown sugar filling’s cloying sweetness. A spoonful of apple cider vinegar may not announce itself boldly, but it makes a small splash for brighter, more balanced bakes.</p> <p>For more fall baking inspiration, check out our Fall Flavor Edit.</p> <p>Transform your favorite bread loaf into shareable rolls.</p> <p>Top tips from the Things Bakers Know podcast.</p> <p>See our complete collection of Tips and Techniques posts.</p> <p>A grocery store shortcut for bakery-worthy treats.</p> <p>It's got cinnamon-scented apples, rich vanilla cake, and a sheer sweet glaze.</p> <p>Eschew classic crust and enter a diverse world of beloved fruit desserts.</p> <p>Facebook TikTok Instagram Threads Pinterest LinkedIn YouTube Reddit Substack</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/blog/2026/09/24/apple-cider-vinegar-recipes" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9739"> <h2>#9739. AnyProfile</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p><p> Free open-source antidetect browser for Mac & Windows </p> <p> <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/products/anyprofile?utm_campaign=producthunt-atom-posts-feed&utm_medium=rss-feed&utm_source=producthunt-atom-posts-feed">Discussion</a> | <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/r/p/1316502?app_id=339">Link</a> </p></p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/products/anyprofile" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9737"> <h2>#9737. What is high-extraction flour, exactly?  : A baker’s guide to our new T85 Baker's Reserve Bread Flour.</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/sites/default/files/2026-09/400968%20Baker%27s%20Reserve%20Bread%20Flour_Spring%20Lifestyle%20Direct_2027_Shot%201_H_2674.jpg" alt="What is high-extraction flour, exactly?  : A baker’s guide to our new T85 Baker's Reserve Bread Flour." style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>High-extraction flour is a technical term that often prompts a lot of confusion from those unfamiliar with it. But with the debut of our new high-extraction flour, known as Baker’s Reserve Bread Flour, we’re breaking down just what it is and why it's a great choice for avid bread makers.</p> <p>The extraction rate of a flour refers to how much of the original grain — the bran, germ, and endosperm — ends up in the final flour. A high-extraction flour typically has an extraction rate of about 80% to 90%, meaning some of the bran and germ have been sifted out, but it still retains much of the original grain. Our Baker’s Reserve Bread Flour is a T85 flour, meaning its extraction rate is 85%.</p> <p>To put that in perspective, whole wheat flour has an extraction rate of 100%; it retains the entirety of the grain, including the bran, germ, and endosperm.</p> <p>High-extraction flour falls between white and whole wheat flour. It’s lighter and less coarse than whole wheat flour because some of the bran has been sifted out, but it still retains more flavor, nutrients, and color than white flour, since it retains much of the original grain.</p> <p>High-extraction flour is popular for artisan bread baking because it offers a balance of nutrition and good gluten development. It’s great for rustic loaves, baguettes, and pizza dough, and particularly well-suited for sourdough baking because it strikes a balance between flavor, nutrition, fermentation, and dough strength.</p> <p>You can substitute our Baker’s Reserve Bread Flour 1:1 for bread flour (by weight or volume) in artisanal bread recipes; it can also be used 1:1 to replace the total flour in recipes that call for a combination of all-purpose and whole wheat flour. If you're subbing Baker’s Reserve Bread Flour for all-purpose flour in a bread recipe, you may find you need to add slightly more liquid to the recipe.</p> <p>Bread bakers love high-extraction flour for artisan bread and sourdough because it offers the flavor and nutrition of whole grain flour; the stronger gluten development and more open crumb you get from white flour; and better fermentation from the minerals present in the bran and germ, which feed the wild yeast and lactic acid bacteria in sourdough starter, promoting more active fermentation.</p> <p>If you want a loaf of bread that’s more flavorful and nutritious than bread made with exclusively white flour, but that still rises high and has an open crumb, high-extraction flour is a great choice.</p> <p>Yes — in fact, it’s a great choice for feeding starter because of the sourdough-friendly minerals present in the flour, which boost activity in your starter.</p> <p>Yes! T85 is a French specification that refers to the extraction rate (85%) of the flour. Our Baker’s Reserve Bread Flour is a T85 flour, meaning the extraction rate is 85%. If you have a recipe that calls for T85, this flour is the perfect choice.</p> <p>Find our high-extraction Baker’s Reserve Bread Flour online.</p> <p>Cover photo by Patrick Marinello; food styling by Yekaterina Boytsova.</p> <p>Transform your favorite bread loaf into shareable rolls.</p> <p>Top tips from the Things Bakers Know podcast.</p> <p>See our complete collection of Story posts.</p> <p>Why a gas oven may be interfering with your go-to steaming method.</p> <p>Don’t fall for this classic sourdough starter trick.</p> <p>Facebook TikTok Instagram Threads Pinterest LinkedIn YouTube Reddit Substack</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/blog/2026/09/28/what-is-high-extraction-flour" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9736"> <h2>#9736. Hollr</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p><p> Push-to-talk for your family, on iPhone and Apple Watch </p> <p> <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/products/hollr-3?utm_campaign=producthunt-atom-posts-feed&utm_medium=rss-feed&utm_source=producthunt-atom-posts-feed">Discussion</a> | <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/r/p/1320275?app_id=339">Link</a> </p></p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/products/hollr-3" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9734"> <h2>#9734. This Breakfast Addition Sharpens Memory Later In The Day</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.spring.org.uk/images/brain-walnuts-1.jpg" alt="This Breakfast Addition Sharpens Memory Later In The Day" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>A simple breakfast addition improved reaction times, but its effects on memory took a more complicated turn.</p> <p>A simple breakfast addition improved reaction times, but its effects on memory took a more complicated turn.</p> <p>Adding walnuts to breakfast could help people respond faster on mental tasks and learn information more effectively later in the day.</p> <p>A generous handful produced small cognitive benefits over the following six hours, although memory performance varied with the timing of the tests.</p> <p>Walnuts may influence how the brain directs attention and obtains the energy needed for demanding mental work.</p> <p>Professor Claire Williams, study co-author, said:</p> <p>“A handful of walnuts with breakfast could give young adults a mental edge when they need to perform at the top of their game.”</p> <p>The research involved over 30 healthy young adults aged 18–30, who ate two different breakfasts on separate visits to the laboratory.</p> <p>One contained 50 g of crushed walnuts mixed into muesli and vanilla yoghurt, while the other contained no nuts.</p> <p>The breakfasts contained almost identical calorie and fat totals, with butter added to the comparison meal to help achieve this match.</p> <p>Participants completed tests before breakfast and again two, four and six hours afterwards, while researchers also recorded their brain activity.</p> <p>After the walnut breakfast, participants responded faster on tasks involving attention, resisting distractions and switching between different mental rules.</p> <p>These abilities form part of executive function, which helps us control our responses and adapt to changing demands.</p> <p>The differences were modest, averaging around eight milliseconds on the attention test and 22 milliseconds when switching between rules.</p> <p>Whether improvements of this size would make a noticeable difference outside the laboratory remains uncertain.</p> <p>The memory findings were more complicated.</p> <p>Two hours after eating walnuts, participants performed slightly worse when repeatedly learning and recalling a list of words.</p> <p>By six hours, however, the pattern had reversed, with better performance after walnuts than after the comparison breakfast.</p> <p>One possibility is that walnuts helped protect learning performance as the testing day wore on.</p> <p>Repeated mental effort can make it harder to take in new information, so preserving the ability to learn could be useful even without improving every aspect of memory.</p> <p>However, participants did not report feeling less mentally fatigued after walnuts, leaving this explanation unconfirmed.</p> <p>Another possibility is that some benefits emerged gradually as nutrients were absorbed and processed.</p> <p>Walnuts contain omega-3 fats, protein and plant compounds called polyphenols, which could contribute individually or together.</p> <p>Electrical recordings revealed differences in frontal and parietal brain activity after the two breakfasts.</p> <p>These regions contribute to attention, memory and the control of behaviour.</p> <p>The changes may indicate that walnuts altered how mental resources were allocated during the tests, although they do not establish precisely why performance improved.</p> <p>Blood samples also showed slightly higher glucose availability and lower concentrations of circulating free fatty acids after walnuts.</p> <p>Greater glucose availability might help fuel demanding mental work.</p> <p>The study was published in the journal Food & Function (Bell et al., 2025).</p> <p>Psychologist, Jeremy Dean, PhD is the founder and author of PsyBlog. He holds a doctorate in psychology from University College London and two other advanced degrees in psychology. He has been writing about scientific research on PsyBlog since 2004. View all posts by Dr Jeremy Dean</p> <p>Join the free PsyBlog mailing list. Backspin</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p><p> Learn to DJ in your browser, on real vinyl decks </p> <p> <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/products/backspin?utm_campaign=producthunt-atom-posts-feed&utm_medium=rss-feed&utm_source=producthunt-atom-posts-feed">Discussion</a> | <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/r/p/1322372?app_id=339">Link</a> </p></p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/products/backspin" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9732"> <h2>#9732. The 12 best recipes to bake in October: It’s peak baking season — here’s what to make.</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/sites/default/files/2026-09/Pumpkin-Milk-Bread_2026_Lifestyle_H_3153.jpg" alt="The 12 best recipes to bake in October: It’s peak baking season — here’s what to make." style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>What do jobs, school, sports practices, and commuting have in common? They all prevent us from baking as much or as often as we’d like. But when we do get the chance, we want a slam-dunk recipe — or 12. Here’s a dozen of the favorite fall recipes we’ll be making this month: from pumpkin cake bars to spooky fudge brownies to a crowd-pleasing vegetarian quiche.</p> <p>It’s the Great Pumpkin, Charlie Brown! Only this version comes in cake form. The decoration is deceptively easy: Stack two small Bundts, frost the entire thing, and add a chocolate-dipped ice cream cone for the stem.</p> <p>Get the recipe: The Great Pumpkin Bundt Cake</p> <p>To make this recipe, you’ll need: Golden Wheat Flour and Pumpkin Pie Spice</p> <p>If you like this recipe, you may also like: Pumpkin Espresso Bundt Cake, Gluten-Free Pumpkin Cake</p> <p>To make this recipe, you’ll need:  Black Cocoa and Supernatural Plant-Based Food Colors</p> <p>These bite-sized pies are a charming addition to any occasion. The boiled cider and spices in the filling ensure a full depth of apple flavor for maximum fall vibes. If you're tight on time, swap the lattice treatment for a buttery crumb topping instead.</p> <p>To make this recipe, you’ll need: Boiled Cider and Apple Pie Spice</p> <p>If you like this recipe, you may also like: Apple Pie Bars, Tiny Apple Tarts for Two</p> <p>Step aside, soup: Butternut squash truly shines in this autumnal quiche. Caramelized onions finished with balsamic vinegar and fresh baby spinach round out the filling, while our Classic Single Pie Crust recipe ensures a tender, golden crust. Elevate the edges with the pie crust decorating technique of your choice.</p> <p>Get the recipe: Roasted Butternut Squash & Spinach Quiche</p> <p>To make this recipe, you’ll need: 9" Pie Pan</p> <p>If you like this recipe, you may also like: Vegetable Quiche, Delicata Squash Galette with Cheese and Herbs</p> <p>Ready to test the theory that only white flour can make rolls light and fluffy? A bit of bread flour and vital wheat gluten give these whole wheat rolls a lofty rise, while the milk, butter, and honey create a plush crumb that stays soft for days. Add a salted honey butter wash to the tops of a freshly baked batch, and you may not have any leftover.</p> <p>Get the recipe: Super-Soft Whole Wheat Rolls</p> <p>To make this recipe, you’ll need: Golden Wheat Flour and Bread Flour</p> <p>If you like this recipe, you may also like: Whole Grain Dinner Rolls, Soft White Dinner Rolls</p> <p>"Tassie" means "small cup" in Scottish, and these dainty pecan pies pack a nutty punch. The cream cheese pastry crust is cut into rounds and placed in a mini muffin pan before the pecan pie filling is spooned into each well. With only 30 minutes of hands-on time, these two dozen tassies come together quickly on a crisp fall afternoon.</p> <p>To make this recipe, you’ll need: Mini Muffin Pan</p> <p>If you like this recipe, you may also like: Easy Pecan Pie Bars, Old-Fashioned Pecan Pie</p> <p>Need a spooky treat, stat? You can transform a plain batch of brownies into a Halloween-themed dessert in a pinch. A simple piping technique creates a spider web effect and adds a touch of rich tang to chocolatey brownies.</p> <p>To make this recipe, you’ll need: 9" x 13" Pan</p> <p>If you like this recipe, you may also like: Fudge Brownies, Chocolate Cheesecake Brownies</p> <p>You’ll notice a lot of similarities between this pumpkin cake and carrot cake: moist, spiced cake, toasted walnuts, and rich cream cheese frosting. These bars are great for delighting a crowd, as this recipe yields three to four dozen bars, depending on how big you slice them. You can easily make them gluten-free, too.</p> <p>Get the recipe: Pumpkin Cake Bars with Cream Cheese Frosting</p> <p>To make this recipe, you’ll need: Pumpkin Pie Spice and Maple Syrup</p> <p>If you like this recipe, you may also like: Pumpkin Spice Latte Bars, Chocolate-Pumpkin Crumb Cake</p> <p>'Tis the season for hand pies to be mummified! A shortening-based pie crust helps the lattice strips stay together, while jam or pie filling allows for customizable flavors. Pop on a few sugar eyes, and you'll be sure to have treats instead of tricks.</p> <p>To make this recipe, you’ll need: Double Pastry Wheel or Pizza Cutter</p> <p>If you like this recipe, you may also like: Flaky Apple Hand Pies, Autumn Apple Turnovers</p> <p>With a luxuriously creamy maple filling and a buttery pecan crust, this cheesecake balances richness with subtle flavors. Meanwhile, the candied pecan garnish adds visual interest and a complementary crunch. Be sure to leave time for an overnight chill and keep your cheesecake from cracking with these tips. (Find more seasonal maple recipes in our Fall Flavor Edit.)</p> <p>To make this recipe, you’ll need: Springform Pan</p> <p>If you like this recipe, you may also like: Caramel Pecan Cheesecake, Maple Cream Pie</p> <p>No need to choose between chocolate or caramel; these cupcakes bring both bold flavors together in a luscious combination. Making caramel from scratch is worth it for the irreplaceable flavor, and those few extra steps are easily done ahead of time. Substitute in Gluten-Free Measure for Measure Flour to make these cupcakes gluten-free. (Find more seasonal caramel recipes in our Fall Flavor Edit.)</p> <p>Get the recipe: Chocolate Cupcakes with Whipped Caramel Frosting</p> <p>To make this recipe, you’ll need: Muffin Pan and Pastry Brush</p> <p>If you like this recipe, you may also like: Chocolate Cupcakes with Pecan Caramel , S’more Cupcakes</p> <p>This milk bread incorporates all the flavor and color of pumpkin, while still keeping an airy texture. You can shape the dough into pull-apart rolls or a loaf, and topping with a milk wash and pumpkin seeds adds a nutty crunch. Wrap it well at room temperature, and this bread will stay soft for days.</p> <p>To make this recipe, you’ll need: Round Pan or Loaf Pan</p> <p>If you like this recipe, you may also like: Japanese Milk Bread, Pumpkin Yeast Bread</p> <p>Cover photo by Patrick Marinello; food styling by Kaitlin Wayne.</p> <p>Transform your favorite bread loaf into shareable rolls.</p> <p>Top tips from the Things If so, then you should consider using an AI content generator. To help you make the best decision, we have compiled a list of the top 10 AI content generator tools that you should use in 2022.</span></p><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">So, without further ado, let’s get started!</span></p><p><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><br /></span></p><h4 style="text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">1. <a href="http://links.crunchhype.com/jasper" rel="nofollow" target="_blank">Jasper Ai</a>(Formerly known as Jarvis)</span></h4><div class="separator" style="clear: both; margin-right: 1em;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><img alt="jasper content generator tool" border="0" height="304" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEjsMf3I0uZly1TdMCGIh0s7GNHgd_Kdr3_WlMtpnboIYU2NOTVz7vGSmPNONCiV5aNZtGdynGK2yAtMNoVzZsgwu6lSLJOeUAcxjSjJ-Tde6dRTM0hJZ9_DEUsW6A1ZuF-1NldLETWqC36DM5o6N5NBTq_hFqY2o91cQ_hU1ziht2JUlID0f-OwyklEkQ/w640-h304/jasper-ai-free-trial-600x285-min.png" title="jasper" width="640" /></span></a></div><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><br /></span><div><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><br /></span></div><div><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"><span><!--more--></span>Jasper is a content writing and content generation tool that uses artificial intelligence to identify the best words and sentences for your writing style and medium in the most efficient, quick, and accessible way.</span></div><h4 style="text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Features</span></h4><p></p><ul style="text-align: left;"><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;"> It's trusted by 50,000+ marketers for creating engaging marketing campaigns, ad copy, blog posts, and articles within minutes which would traditionally take hours or days. Special Features:</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Comfortaa;">Blog posts have been optimized for search engines and rank high on Google and other search engines.
