Upgrade Your Next Grilled Cheese With A Rich & Creamy Store-Bought Spread</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.foodrepublic.com/img/gallery/upgrade-your-next-grilled-cheese-with-a-rich-creamy-store-bought-spread/l-intro-1794837328.jpg" alt="Upgrade Your Next Grilled Cheese With A Rich & Creamy Store-Bought Spread" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.</p> <p>The essence of the best grilled cheese lies in the delicious combination of melted cheese and crisped bread. There are many methods to accomplish such a pairing, with plenty of tips to give you the best results imaginable. If you're after a version that's especially ooey-gooey, try making the sandwich with cheddar cheese spread.</p> <p>Available from several brands at widespread grocery stores like Walmart, cheddar cheese spread is essentially cheddar mixed with butter. The foodstuff is easily spreadable on bread and melts when it's heated, making a grilled cheese with a pleasantly runny interior. While it's creamier than classic cheddar, the flavor is no afterthought, with this cheese's sharpness still perceptible.</p> <p>Using butter alongside cheese is common in grilled cheese recipes; the spread lets you conveniently lather on both components at once. The fat enhances the bread's crispiness, all while retaining a moist interior. As a sole filling, the spread turns the dish luxuriously decadent — but complemented with a few slices of cheese, it's a grilled cheese rendition to remember.</p> <p>There are many international grilled cheese styles to explore; cheddar cheese spread fits into a wide range of renditions. Combined with a store-bought loaf of sourdough and sliced cheddar, the spread makes a mouth-watering classic. However, you can consider layering in other ingredients, too — thereby making a cheddar grilled cheese with a twist.</p> <p>For example, the cheese's sharpness welcomes a sweet contrast. Spread a jam or jelly into the sandwich, whether a rich fig jam, tart cranberry preserves, or a sweet blackberry jam. For a sweet touch with less sugar, you could also use fresh fruits to upgrade any grilled cheese; the spread would go great with apples, for example, as apples and cheddar are a match made in sandwich heaven. And you could also consider leaning into the spice, smearing on spicy brown mustard or hot pepper jelly for a light dose of heat.</p> <p>Consider trying out other ingredient add-ins, too. Caramelized onions will lend a grilled cheese a subtle nutty sweetness, while bacon bits bring a savory touch. Cheddar cheese spreads allow the many different flavors to come together, letting you easily craft a sandwich to your tastes.</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.foodrepublic.com/2317501/upgrade-grilled-cheese-rich-creamy-store-bought-spread-cheddar/" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9687"> <h2>#9687. How to proof bread in the oven: Common challenge, simple solution.</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/sites/default/files/2026-09/how%20to%20proof%20bread%20in%20oven.jpg" alt="How to proof bread in the oven: Common challenge, simple solution." style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>During proofing, bread and other yeasted doughs do best in a temperature-controlled, humid, draft-free environment. Your kitchen counter may not cut it (especially in colder months), but is there a corner of your kitchen that fits that description? Yes, your oven — and you don’t even need to fire it up!</p> <p>Yeast dough is happiest when rising at temperatures between 75°F and 78°F. It will certainly rise in cooler or warmer temperatures. But for most doughs, that range is optimum for both yeast development and bread flavor.</p> <p>Your oven’s interior will pretty much mirror room temperature. And depending on the time of year (or how much you use air conditioning), that temperature could be pretty cool—too cool for yeast’s comfort.</p> <p>To get the oven up to that ideal proofing temperature, people often turn to a couple of different methods. I decided to try a bunch of them to see which is best — and helpfully, there was a clear winner.</p> <p>It’s tempting to simply preheat the oven for a minute or so to warm its interior; but not only is this hit-and-miss (How long should I leave it on? Will the oven get too hot?), it’s ineffective; the heat quickly dissipates once you turn the oven off.</p> <p>Enter your oven light. When turned on, your oven light’s slow, gentle heat will gradually warm the oven to the desired temperature. After trying a number of different methods for proofing bread in the oven, including several listed below, this was my clear favorite because it created the ideal temperature (not too hot, not too cold), maintained that temperature for several hours, and was essentially failproof (no overshooting the temp, for example!).</p> <p>It can take your oven a while to reach the desired temperature, especially if your kitchen is cold to begin with. With so many variables — season, climate, kitchen, oven — you’ll want to do a simple experiment to determine your own best method for turning your oven into an effective, efficient proof box:</p> <p>Take your oven’s temperature before turning on the light. Then turn on the light and measure the temperature again at 15-minute intervals, to see just how quickly the light warms things up. For reference, the light in my electric oven takes about an hour to raise the oven’s interior temperature by 10 degrees, and another hour to raise it an additional five degrees; your results will probably vary a bit.</p> <p>Warm your oven to about 80°F before turning off the light. Over the next couple of hours, the temperature will gradually drift down by about 10 degrees, giving your rising dough plenty of time in and around that 75°F to 78°F sweet spot.</p> <p>Once you know how to warm your oven using only its lightbulb, think about maintaining humidity: Dry dough can develop a tough skin, which inhibits rising.</p> <p>If you’re proofing dough in a bowl (or later, a shaped loaf in a pan), cover it with a clear plastic shower cap or reusable plastic bowl cover. Whatever you use, make sure it's large enough to form a “poof” on top, so the cover doesn’t touch the rising dough.</p> <p>For shaped rolls (or anything else in a large, flat pan), use an extra-large shower cap; or simply drape the pan with well-greased plastic wrap, waxed paper, or parchment.</p> <p>What if your oven doesn’t have a light, the lightbulb only lights when you open the oven door, or it’s a “cool” LED bulb?</p> <p>Then your best bet is a pan of boiling water set on the lowest rack, which will both warm and humidify your oven’s interior. Place the bread dough on the oven’s middle rack; no need to cover it.  Set a shallow pan (e.g., 9" x 13" pan) on the lower rack, and add four cups of boiling water. Quickly close the oven door.</p> <p>Your oven’s temperature will immediately rise by about 30 degrees, which will probably be warmer than you want. Cool it down by opening the door wide for about five minutes; the temperature should drop about 15 degrees.</p> <p>As the water in the oven cools, the air around it cools, too. But it happens so gradually that your oven should still remain sufficiently warm for the one to two hours your bread typically needs to rise. For longer-rising breads, simply switch out the cool water with another pan of hot water, if necessary.</p> <p>Some ovens actually have a proof setting or proofing drawer. I don’t always love using this setting, though: Most are programmed to temperatures ranging from 90°F to 100°F, far warmer than yeast dough’s optimal 75°F to 78°F. For best results, figure out how long it takes to reach about 80°F, then turn it off.</p> <p>Tip #1: If you have to open the oven door to check your rising dough, don’t worry. Unlike the huge 15- to 20-degree drop you experience when opening a fully heated oven, the temperature inside your light- or steam-warmed oven will only drop by a degree or two.</p> <p>Tip #2: Typically, you don’t preheat your oven with rising dough inside. So when your dough is close to fully risen, remove it from the oven and set it somewhere safe. (If there’s room, the top of your fridge is both warm and out of harm’s way.) Timed just right, your bread will be perfectly proved by the time the oven finishes preheating.</p> <p>Tip #3: To prevent someone from killing your rising dough by turning on the oven (say, to warm their leftover pizza), write “NO!” on a sticky note and affix it to the oven’s start button. Really!</p> <p>For the highly passionate bread baker (or a small baking business), an electronic proof box like the Brod & Taylor Proofer Pro is a step up from proofing dough in the oven. It controls temperature with exquisite precision, from cold-proofing (down to 41°F) for those overnight ferments up to 122°F for an express warmup, all while ensuring perfect humidity. Wi-Fi and programmable timers let you control your dough’s development for up to eight days. It’s literally set it and forget it — the process is simple, but the results are simply amazing.</p> <p>Still looking for a warm, draft-free spot for your rising bread dough? Think beyond your oven to other major appliances: Both your clothes dryer and dishwasher can double as a proof box!</p> <p>Cover photo by Mark Weinberg; food styling by Liz Neily.</p> <p>Transform your favorite bread loaf into shareable rolls.</p> <p>Top tips from the Things Bakers Know podcast.</p> <p>See our complete collection of Tips and Techniques posts.</p> <p>Dough temperature is key to achieving consistently great results in your bread baking.</p> <p>Facebook TikTok Instagram Threads Pinterest LinkedIn YouTube Reddit Substack</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/blog/2026/10/23/how-to-proof-bread-in-oven" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9686"> <h2>#9686. Webless Agents</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p><p> Agents you want to put in front of customers </p> <p> <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/products/webless?utm_campaign=producthunt-atom-posts-feed&utm_medium=rss-feed&utm_source=producthunt-atom-posts-feed">Discussion</a> | <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/r/p/1307253?app_id=339">Link</a> </p></p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/products/webless" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9685"> <h2>#9685. Creavit Studio 4.0</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p><p> Screen recording, iPhone camera and cinematic demos for Mac </p> <p> <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/products/creavit-studio?utm_campaign=producthunt-atom-posts-feed&utm_medium=rss-feed&utm_source=producthunt-atom-posts-feed">Discussion</a> | <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/r/p/1324705?app_id=339">Link</a> </p></p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/products/creavit-studio" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9684"> <h2>#9684. 22 Recipes To Make With Thanksgiving Leftovers</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.foodrepublic.com/img/gallery/22-recipes-to-make-with-thanksgiving-leftovers/l-intro-1795142749.jpg" alt="22 Recipes To Make With Thanksgiving Leftovers" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>Turkey, ham, mashed potatoes, casseroles, pumpkin, cranberries, stuffing ... the annual fall-flavored feast that we know and love is always a crowd-pleasing holiday meal to look forward to. And one of the best things about Thanksgiving isn't just the meal itself; it's all of the delicious leftovers that inevitably follow.</p> <p>Especially when you're hosting a crowd (which is possible to do stress-free with these tips from Guy Fieri), those leftovers can be abundant. But the beauty is that there's so much more you can do with your Thanksgiving leftovers than just reheat and re-eat. From soups, sandwiches, and snacks that repurpose your ingredients to completely new dishes that transform the original elements of the meal, you can take those leftovers in so many directions.</p> <p>If you're looking for new ideas or creative ways to use up what's left in the fridge, we've got a plethora of recipes to try that'll help you make the most of your Thanksgiving leftovers. (Pro tip: Just don't forget the 2-2-2 rule with your leftovers to ensure food safety.)</p> <p>Whether you enjoyed some mac & cheese on Thanksgiving Day or not, this recipe is a whole new twist on the classic that infuses the beloved dish with holiday flavor. It's honestly a little shocking how many leftover ingredients manage to make their way into this one recipe, but when you think about it ... how could it not taste good?</p> <p>This Thanksgiving Leftover Macaroni & Cheese incorporates three different types of cheese — fontina, cheddar, and mascarpone — to make the cheese sauce. Then come the Thanksgiving leftovers that get folded into the dish: shredded turkey meat, sweet potatoes, peas, and pasta. After it's baked, the whole thing is topped off with some cranberry sauce to bring the Thanksgiving flavors home.</p> <p>Recipe: Thanksgiving Leftover Macaroni & Cheese</p> <p>Now, this is a fun one — it's Thanksgiving dinner in burger form! Not only can you use that leftover stuffing, but this recipe also calls for turkey meat, gravy, and cranberry sauce, so this one wins for maximizing whatever's taking up space in the fridge. And it's incredibly tasty, too.</p> <p>The "burger" is a combination of stuffing, turkey, eggs, and milk in patty form. The patty is then griddled in some butter and topped off with cranberry sauce, gravy, and goat cheese to create a burger that'll leave you stuffed in the best way.</p> <p>Recipe: Leftover Thanksgiving Stuffing Burger</p> <p>Okay, a turkey cheesesteak might seem a little contradictory, but this one's worth entertaining when it comes to making the most of your Thanksgiving leftovers. You won't just knock out the leftover turkey, but also any leftover gravy with this Thanksgiving Leftover Turkey Cheesesteak.</p> <p>The cheesesteak starts with sautéed sweet onions, and then the turkey (dark meat works great if you have it), gravy, and cornichons are added to the mix before two types of cheese (provolone and American cheese) are melted on top. Everything is stuffed into toasty hoagie rolls to make a saucy, messy, tasty Thanksgiving cheesesteak.</p> <p>Recipe: Thanksgiving Leftover Turkey Cheesesteak</p> <p>Why not whip up the ultimate comfort meal to enjoy the weekend after Thanksgiving? Once the holiday winds down, you can use your leftover turkey (and any extra pumpkin puree you might have lying around) in this Pumpkin and Turkey Chili recipe. This fall take on a classic slow cooker chili recipe incorporates pumpkin puree into the stew along with a blend of warm spices like cinnamon, cloves, and nutmeg.</p> <p>To sub in your already-cooked turkey, just skip the initial step where you'd brown the ground turkey, and instead add some cubed or shredded turkey once your chili is simmering.</p> <p>Making croquettes is a fun and delicious way to use up that leftover turkey. Croquettes actually originated in France as a way to use up leftover meats and vegetables, so they're the perfect way to repurpose those Thanksgiving leftovers.</p> <p>The cheesy croquettes are made by sautéeing mushrooms, onions, and garlic and combining the mixture with cooked turkey, parsley, and mozzarella cheese. They're then shaped into balls, dipped into egg and breadcrumbs, and lightly fried until golden brown and crispy.</p> <p>Recipe: Crispy Turkey and Cheese Croquettes</p> <p>Shepherd's pie is a great follow-up recipe to Thanksgiving if you need a way to reuse copious amounts of mashed potatoes, because that iconic mashed potato topping makes shepherd's pie what it is. This particular recipe is made with ground lamb and vegetables like corn, peas, and carrots as the base of the pie, but you could easily sub in your leftover turkey as well if you want to knock out two leftovers in one go.</p> <p>Either way, this Simple Shepherd's Pie is even easier to make since the mashed potatoes are already done. All you need to do is assemble, bake, and enjoy ... or if you're feeling ambitious, you can try one of these 15 secret ingredients to make your Shepherd's Pie the best it can be.</p> <p>Bought too many potatoes on your Thanksgiving grocery run? This casserole will come in handy for those extra ingredients. The simple, easy-to-make dish combines potatoes, onions, bacon, and thyme with cream, chicken stock, and cheese. Everything gets baked until it's melty and delicious, making a perfect side dish to pair with any leftover meat from the holiday.</p> <p>This recipe uses blue cheese, which complements the bacon, but you can feel free to use any cheese you like (cheddar, mozzarella, or even Gruyère would all work great).</p> <p>This comforting soup brings together many ingredients that were most likely on your Thanksgiving shopping list, including carrots, apples, potatoes, and pecans. It's the perfect meal to throw together that'll make use of all of those extra groceries that you're not sure what to do with. Carrots and apples may not be your first thoughts as the base of a soup, but trust us, this comforting soup recipe is a (somewhat unexpected) winner.</p> <p>All you need to do is cook your vegetables down with plenty of flavorful herbs and spices like cinnamon, nutmeg, ginger, and fresh thyme. Add your stock, blend until smooth, and finish off with the cream for a nutty and rich yet soothing soup that you can work your way through all week.</p> <p>For all those who may have purchased some fresh pumpkins for your Thanksgiving pie but didn't get around to using all of it, we've got just the recipe. As a bonus, it'll use up those extra potatoes, too!</p> <p>Put a fall spin on a classic potato gratin by slicing your pumpkin into pieces or rounds the same size as your potatoes. The cream mixture, which is made up of heavy cream, garlic, thyme, rosemary, and salt, gets layered with your pumpkin and potatoes; then everything is covered with grated Swiss cheese and baked longer than you may think until the whole dish is bubbly, browned, and cheesy.</p> <p>Whether you've got some extra sweet potatoes lying around from a casserole side dish or a sweet potato pie, this Sweet Potato Tarte Tatin is a delicious way to use them up. And with a little puff pastry, this dish looks impressive but doesn't take long to make a classic tarte tatin.</p> <p>The trick is making the caramel element; once you've gotten that down, the rest is smooth sailing. Your homemade caramel will come together with sliced sweet potatoes and a puff pastry covering to produce an irresistible starchy take on the tarte tatin.</p> <p>Similar to the tarte tatin, you can use a store-bought dough (this time, paper-thin Greek phyllo pastry) to keep this dessert simple. Baklava is typically made with nuts, but this recipe replaces that crunchy ingredient with a smooth pumpkin puree — along with spices like cinnamon, nutmeg, and clove — for a tasty fall twist on this decadent, flaky treat.</p> <p>Baklava involves making a simple syrup of sorts, and then it's all about layering (and this hack for assembling can make your baklava process even quicker). In the end, you'll have an extremely crispy, sweet-yet-spiced dessert born from leftover pumpkin puree.</p> <p>If there's one thing you may not have thought to do with your leftover pumpkin and cranberries, it might be homemade liqueur. It might seem a little extreme, but it's not as complicated as it sounds, and you will be rewarded with an ingredient that'll help level up your baking and cocktails for many weeks to come.</p> <p>In short, the process just involves cooking down your chosen ingredient with sugar, then adding a high-proof liquor like vodka, and then straining it and letting it sit. That's it!</p> <p>Recipe: Cranberry Liqueur and Pumpkin Liqueur</p> <p>If you didn't quite make as much apple pie filling as you planned, don't worry — this one's for you. It's basically a shortcut apple pie filling that you can throw on some ice cream, douse in whipped cream, or simply enjoy on its own.</p> <p>This Sweet Spiced Baked Apples recipe is one of the easiest ways to make use of all of those leftover apples. Any apples will do: Honeycrisp, Fuji, Pink Lady, you name it. All you need to do is bake them with an undeniably delicious mixture of brown sugar, walnuts, butter, and spices. It's so simple, and so satisfying.</p> <p>Sticking with those leftover apples, this recipe will make a fantastic breakfast or brunch in the days following Thanksgiving. The Americanized origins of Dutch baby pancakes are a bit complicated, but long story short, this creation is essentially a giant, skillet-baked pancake. And it's a great go-to dish to capitalize on your extra apples, because you most likely have everything else you need stocked in your kitchen.</p> <p>This Dutch baby recipe uses a batter made of flour, milk, eggs, honey, vanilla extract, salt, and melted butter. Next, pour the batter over thinly sliced apples that have been tossed in brown sugar and cinnamon. Everything is then baked together to perfection until your leftover apples turn into puffy, golden goodness.</p> <p>This is a unique and flavorful way to use any extra pumpkins you have from the holiday. The bonus? The presentation is impressive, so if you find yourself continuing to host through the weekend, this is another great meal to provide for your guests that will help you repurpose some of your Thanksgiving ingredients.</p> <p>With everything from coconut milk and ground pork to ginger, soy sauce, and water chestnuts, this rice dish includes a lot of really interesting ingredients that may not seem like they belong together, but they all unite to build a warm, aromatic meal. Just trust the process, serve it up inside a pumpkin, and watch your guests marvel.</p> <p>Recipe: Stuffed Pumpkin With Aromatic Rice</p> <p>Although this recipe includes a lot of similar ingredients as the above (rice, pumpkin, nuts), the elements come together in a totally different way to create a totally different dish: a warmly spiced, sweet rice pudding that'll taste just like your Thanksgiving pumpkin pie.</p> <p>The dessert is made with Arborio rice, almond milk, maple syrup, pumpkin puree, vanilla, and spices — everything gets simmered together until it thickens into a pudding, then chilled and served with glazed pecans for extra crunch.</p> <p>Leftovers truly shine when you use them to build a great sandwich. Meet this Sweet and Savory Monte Cristo Sandwich, which can be made with your leftover Thanksgiving turkey and ham. In addition to the sliced duo of meat, this sandwich features Gruyère cheese, mayo, and raspberry jam (although you can obviously sub in some cranberry sauce if you so please), all stacked between slices of brioche bread.</p> <p>What makes this Monte Cristo extra delicious is the French toast treatment that it gets: Once assembled, the entire sandwich is dipped in a mixture of egg, half-and-half, and nutmeg and lightly fried in butter until golden brown. Oh, it's then topped off with some powdered sugar for good measure.</p> <p>Recipe: Sweet And Savory Monte Cristo Sandwich</p> <p>Here's another fun breakfast recipe to keep things interesting over the holiday weekend! This take on a Croque Madame (a classic French sandwich typically made with ham, cheese, and Mornay sauce and topped with a sunny-side-up egg) creates a "waffled" version of the sandwich by employing a waffle iron as the cooking tool.</p> <p>Where do the leftovers come in? The waffle "batter" is made with your leftover Thanksgiving stuffing, which you'll then combine with milk and eggs. This concoction is then topped with slices of ham and grated cheddar cheese, and finished off with a fried or poached egg. Post-Thanksgiving brunch is served.</p> <p>If you've still got some sweet potatoes left from your holiday shopping, this is another great recipe to make use of them — and it couldn't be simpler. This Sweet Potato and Sausage Hash makes a great breakfast or brunch, and can be topped with some eggs or eaten on its own. And all it takes is six ingredients to get there.</p> <p>The dish starts with some onions and garlic sautéed in butter. These are then combined with cooked Italian sausage and cubed sweet potatoes. Everything is roasted together in a cast-iron skillet, showing how you can make this recipe with minimal effort and maximum tastiness.</p> <p>There are never enough ways to use up those extra potatoes! This time, your floury potatoes like Yukon Golds or Russets take the lead with an herby potato galette. This particular recipe is a crustless galette, so there's no dough necessary, and you only need a handful of ingredients to make it.</p> <p>To make the galette, shred the potatoes, add them to a hot skillet with lots of olive oil and sage, then press them down to help form a natural crust. Cook the potatoes for another 10 minutes as butter is added to the pan, then flip the whole thing and cook it on the other side. The result is a crispy potato pancake that's golden on the outside, soft on the inside, and delicious all the way around.</p> <p>It's the ultimate Thanksgiving grilled cheese, so you don't want to pass this one up. You can make use of several leftover ingredients for this sandwich, both savory and sweet, such as extra apples and leftover ham.</p> <p>Apple butter is spread across two slices of sourdough bread, and then layered with Brie, diced ham, and diced apples before the sandwich is toasted in butter. This simply isn't your average grilled cheese sandwich; you also get bonus points if you can pair it with some butternut squash soup.</p> <p>Recipe: Sweet and Savory Brie and Apple Butter Grilled Cheese</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.foodrepublic.com/2322627/thanksgiving-leftover-recipes/" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9683"> <h2>#9683. The Pedalling Prescription: 12 Ways Cycling Can Change Your Mind (P)</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.spring.org.uk/images/cycling-1-2.jpg" alt="The Pedalling Prescription: 12 Ways Cycling Can Change Your Mind (P)" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>From instant cognitive boosts to lasting emotional resilience, cycling offers powerful, science-backed brain benefits.</p> <p>Cycling is widely celebrated for its cardiovascular and physical health benefits, but its effects on the mind may be just as remarkable.</p> <p>Emerging research suggests that pedalling can influence mood, stress, memory, attention and motivation in many different ways.</p> <p>These mental shifts do not follow a single timeline: while some cognitive and emotional benefits appear almost instantly after a few minutes in the saddle, others unfold gradually over weeks or months of regular riding.</p> <p>Here are 12 studies that highlight the remarkable ways cycling can affect your mental health.</p> <p>• Read members-only and premium content • Access courses • Adverts removed • Cancel at any time • 14 day money-back guarantee for new members</p> <p>Psychologist, Jeremy Dean, PhD is the founder and author of PsyBlog. He holds a doctorate in psychology from University College London and two other advanced degrees in psychology. He has been writing about scientific research on PsyBlog since 2004. View all posts by Dr Jeremy Dean</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.spring.org.uk/2026/11/10-cycling.php" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9682"> <h2>#9682. Pushback</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p><p> The flight tracker that knows which lounge you can use </p> <p> <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/products/pushback-flight-tracker?utm_campaign=producthunt-atom-posts-feed&utm_medium=rss-feed&utm_source=producthunt-atom-posts-feed">Discussion</a> | <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/r/p/1323604?app_id=339">Link</a> </p></p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/products/pushback-flight-tracker" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9681"> <h2>#9681. The secret to make-ahead pie crust? Pie crumbs.: Get ahead on your pie baking right now.</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/sites/default/files/2026-10/pie%20crumsb.jpg" alt="The secret to make-ahead pie crust? Pie crumbs.: Get ahead on your pie baking right now." style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>'Tis the season — to start thinking about holiday baking. And while this time of year is full of joy and celebration, it can also be stressful. We’re all searching for ways to get ahead of the curve, and one of the easiest? Make-ahead pie crust, made using pie crumbs.</p> <p>I first learned of this technique from a 90-something friend with whom I love to talk baking. Over lunch one day, something she said about pie captured my attention.</p> <p>"Did you ever hear of pie crumbs?" she asked. I admitted I hadn't — aside from the obvious: the scraps of pie crust left on the plate after the slice is gone. "My mother used to mix flour and salt and lard together to make this crumbly mixture that she'd store in a crock in the cellar. She called them her pie crumbs. When she wanted to make a pie, she'd just scoop out a few handfuls, add water, and roll out her crust."</p> <p>Sounds like a good make-ahead solution for 100 years ago — but now that we have easy access to freezers, why not just make pie dough and freeze it in ready-to-roll disks? A couple of reasons, actually.</p> <p>1) Pie crumbs allow you to make any amount of crust, from mini apple pies to a crust for a deep-dish 10" pie. With frozen disks, you're looking at a standard single crust — not always exactly what you want.</p> <p>2) Pie crumbs save time. Remove however much of the crumbly mixture you need (more on this below) from the freezer, and within 15 minutes the fat is soft enough that you can add water and roll out your crust. Compare that to the hours it takes to thaw and roll a frozen disk of prepared crust — not to mention the elbow grease if your crust isn’t fully thawed.</p> <p>3) Pie crumbs can be more stable in the freezer than pie crust disks. Why? Because without the added water, no ice crystals form. Ice crystals can damage the flour/water matrix, leading to changes in its structure (which can then potentially lead to changes in your pie crust).</p> <p>Oh, and one other reason I like pie crumbs: If my friend's mother used them, they were probably a 19th-century kitchen time-saver. And I love the feeling of preserving and carrying forward our American baking traditions — even something as simple as a shortcut for pie crust.</p> <p>Choose a standard pie crust recipe: Our Classic Double Pie Crust recipe is good choice, but anything that involves cutting fat into flour (lard, shortening, butter, etc.) will work.</p> <p>Mix flour, salt, and shortening and/or butter: Follow your recipe up until all of the fat is incorporated into the flour. You should be left with a bowl of dry, crumbly dough that barely holds together when squeezed. If using butter, you should be able to see visible chunks scattered throughout the dough.</p> <p>Weigh the pie crumbs: If you’re making a large batch of pie crumbs, it’s helpful to weigh and label the total gram amount so that you can easily remove the amount of pie crumbs for a single pie crust as needed. Our Classic Double Pie Crust makes 488 grams of pie crumbs; that means 244 grams per single pie crust. Label these amounts on your freezer storage bag.</p> <p>Bag, label, and freeze the crumbs: Seal pie crumbs in an airtight, freezer-safe bag and place in the freezer, preferably in the back where it won't be subject to warm air wafting over it each time you open the freezer door.</p> <p>Scoop crumbs out of the bag into a bowl: Whether one crust, two crusts, or one and a half, do the math and measure the crumbs based on your recorded gram amounts.</p> <p>Let the crumbs thaw for 15 to 20 minutes or so: Wait until the butter chunks feel barely pliable in your fingers.</p> <p>Add water and mix: Add water based on your original recipe amount, or just enough water to make a chunky mass when mixed. Squeeze and knead the dough briefly; all you're doing here is bringing the chunks together into one solid piece of dough.</p> <p>Roll the dough, place in a pan, and bake accordingly: From here, your pie crust is the same as any fresh-made crust and can be filled and baked or prebaked for a no-bake filling. (Bonus: Because the crumbs were frozen and remain cold as you work with them, there's no need to chill your rolled-out crust before filling and/or baking.)</p> <p>Fairly indefinitely, though the longer they're frozen, the more chance they have both to absorb freezer odors, and for the fats to start to go off. I've also found that, after about two weeks in the freezer, I need to add a touch more water than usual to bring the dough together — due to the drying effects inherent in freezing.</p> <p>With pie season hard upon us, now's the time to try pie crumbs for make-ahead pie crust. Or maybe you have another old-fashioned pie trick up your sleeve? Share your favorite tips in the comments, below.</p> <p>For detailed ingredient amounts for the crust demonstrated above, see our recipe for Classic Double Pie Crust.</p> <p>And if you're looking for additional time-saving ways to use your freezer in the run-up to the holidays, check out our recipe for Homemade Brown and Serve Rolls and Apple Pie with Make-Ahead Filling.</p> <p>Cover photo and food styling by Liz Neily.</p> <p>Transform your favorite bread loaf into shareable rolls.</p> <p>Top tips from the Things Bakers Know podcast.</p> <p>See our complete collection of Tips and Techniques posts.</p> <p>Top tips from the Things Bakers Know podcast.</p> <p>Mini pies may be the secret to a stress-free celebration.</p> <p>Because we're all wondering what to do with our apple and pumpkin pies.</p> <p>Facebook TikTok Instagram Threads Pinterest LinkedIn YouTube Reddit Substack</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/blog/2026/10/26/make-ahead-pie-crust" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9680"> <h2>#9680. Raccoon Kids</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p><p> Gamify Chores for Kids: no more nagging, just a cute raccoon </p> <p> <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/products/raccoon-kids?utm_campaign=producthunt-atom-posts-feed&utm_medium=rss-feed&utm_source=producthunt-atom-posts-feed">Discussion</a> | <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/r/p/1322851?app_id=339">Link</a> </p></p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/products/raccoon-kids" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9679"> <h2>#9679. The State With The Most Wendy's Locations Isn't New York, California, Or Texas</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.foodrepublic.com/img/gallery/the-state-with-the-most-wendys-locations-isnt-new-york-california-or-texas/l-intro-1794926140.jpg" alt="The State With The Most Wendy's Locations Isn't New York, California, Or Texas" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>Wendy's is a beloved chain of fast food restaurants whose square-shaped burger patties are instantly recognizable to many American diners. Founded in 1969 in Columbus, Ohio, the brand is an institution where it was born — yet the Midwestern state doesn't actually have the most locations. Neither do populous hubs like California or New York. Rather, you need to look southeast to the land of orange groves. With 464 restaurants as of November 2026, Florida has more Wendy's locations than any other state in the country.</p> <p>The Sunshine State accounts for roughly 8% of the total number of locations this fast food giant has in the United States, compared to Texas, which has slightly fewer locations at 419. However, if you take population differences into account, there are more restaurants per capita in Florida than in the Lone Star State. This means that Florida residents are more likely to find a Wendy's nearby. Not everything seems to be bigger in Texas, after all, at least when it comes to this fast food chain.</p> <p>Additionally, two Florida cities — Miami and Orlando — are in the top five U.S. cities with the most Wendy's locations (per ScrapeHero). So, whether you're enjoying the nightlife of South Beach or visiting Disney World, you won't be too far from a Jr. Bacon Cheeseburger. Despite Florida's distinction of having the most locations, however, it doesn't have the largest Wendy's in the world. That honor goes to Tbilisi, the capital of Georgia, a country in the Caucasus region.</p> <p>The idea of people vacationing in, moving to, or spending part of the year in Florida is an old trope, and there's a good reason for it. Many Americans see the state as a respite from the cold, and the Sunshine State actually has a long history of being a destination for migrants moving down from northern states, dating back to as early as the 1800s.</p> <p>Interestingly, people from Ohio comprise a large portion of these migrants — in fact, according to USAFacts, more Ohioans moved to Florida than to any other state in 2024. Just like immigrants from other countries, American transplants bring their own cultures that can influence the local culinary scene, and maybe that's why there are so many Wendy's locations in the Sunshine State.</p> <p>Considering how the brand was founded in the Buckeye State, perhaps the many transplants brought their taste for the chain's iconic baked potatoes, chili, and square burgers with them. After all, Ohio has the third-largest number of Wendy's restaurants and has more locations per capita than Florida. It might seem like mere coincidence until you take into account the fact that Florida is also home to another Buckeye institution, Skyline Chili, and it's the only state outside the Midwest where the chain is present.</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.foodrepublic.com/2318078/state-with-most-wendys-locations-not-new-york-california-texas/" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9678"> <h2>#9678. oovi</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p><p> Your own team of AI on your desktop </p> <p> <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/products/oovi?utm_campaign=producthunt-atom-posts-feed&utm_medium=rss-feed&utm_source=producthunt-atom-posts-feed">Discussion</a> | <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/r/p/1325665?app_id=339">Link</a> </p></p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/products/oovi" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9677"> <h2>#9677. How I Get Free Traffic from ChatGPT in 2025 (AIO vs SEO)</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>Three weeks ago, I tested something that completely changed how I think about organic traffic. I opened ChatGPT and asked a simple question: "What's the best course on building SaaS with WordPress?" The answer that appeared stopped me cold. My course showed up as the first result, recommended directly by the AI with specific reasons why it was valuable.</p> <p>I hadn't paid for advertising. I hadn't done any special promotion. The AI simply decided my content was the best answer to that question and served it to the user. This wasn't luck or a fluke. When I tested the same query in Perplexity, the same thing happened. My website ranked at the top of AI-generated responses, pulling in free traffic directly from AI models that millions of people now use as their primary search tool.</p> <p>This represents a fundamental shift in how people discover content online. For years, we've optimized for Google's algorithm, carefully crafting meta descriptions and building backlinks to climb traditional search rankings. That work still matters, but a massive new traffic source has emerged that most content creators are completely ignoring. While everyone focuses exclusively on traditional SEO, AI Optimization is quietly becoming one of the most valuable skills for anyone who publishes content online.</p> <p>The opportunity is enormous right now precisely because it's so new. Early adopters are claiming top positions in AI responses while their competitors remain oblivious to this emerging channel. But this window won't stay open forever. As more people recognize the value of appearing in AI results, competition will increase and optimization will become more sophisticated. The time to understand and implement AIO strategies is now, while the landscape is still relatively uncrowded.</p> <p>In this comprehensive guide, I'll show you exactly how AI Optimization works, how it differs from traditional SEO, what specific tactics actually move the needle, and how to track your performance so you know what's working. More importantly, I'll explain why you can't afford to ignore this traffic source if you want to remain visible online as user behavior continues shifting toward AI-powered search.</p> <p>Something profound has changed in how people find information online, and most website owners haven't noticed yet. The change isn't about a new Google algorithm update or a shift in social media platforms. It's about where people go when they have questions that need answering.</p> <p>For twenty years, the pattern was predictable and universal. Someone needs information, they open Google, they type a query, they scan through ten blue links, they click a few results, they piece together answers from multiple sources. This process trained us to optimize for that journey. We focused on ranking in those ten blue links because that's where traffic came from. The entire SEO industry built around understanding and exploiting that single funnel.</p> <p>But look at what's happening now. Someone needs information, they open ChatGPT or Claude or Perplexity, they ask a question in natural language, they receive a comprehensive answer immediately with sources cited. No clicking through multiple websites. No comparing different perspectives. No scanning search results pages. The AI synthesizes information and delivers a direct answer, fundamentally changing the discovery process.</p> <p>The numbers tell the story. ChatGPT reached 100 million users faster than any consumer application in history, hitting that milestone in just two months after launch. By early 2025, ChatGPT alone processes over 10 million queries daily through its web browsing feature. Perplexity has grown to millions of daily users who rely on it as their primary search tool. Google has responded by launching AI Mode, available in over 180 countries, which provides AI-generated answers above traditional search results.</p> <p>These aren't niche tools used by tech enthusiasts. They're mainstream applications that everyday people now use for research, planning, learning, and decision-making. When someone searches for "best productivity apps for small teams," they're increasingly likely to ask an AI rather than Google. When a business owner needs to understand a technical topic, they're prompting Claude instead of reading blog posts. When students research topics for papers, they're querying Perplexity instead of clicking through search results.</p> <p>This behavioral shift creates a new visibility challenge. Your content might rank perfectly on Google, but if it's invisible to AI models when they're formulating answers, you're missing an enormous and growing segment of potential traffic. The users who discover information through AI tools never even see your traditional search rankings because they never visit a search results page.</p> <p>The problem compounds because AI search is still in its explosive growth phase. Usage is doubling and tripling year over year as more people discover these tools and integrate them into their daily workflows. The traffic opportunity today is significant, but it's tiny compared to what it will become in the next few years as AI search becomes default behavior for entire demographics.</p> <p>AIO stands for AI Optimization, and it represents the practice of optimizing your content to appear in AI-generated responses when people query language models. Think of it as SEO's younger sibling, similar in purpose but different in execution because the underlying mechanisms for how AI models select and cite sources differ fundamentally from how Google ranks web pages.</p> <p>Traditional SEO focuses on signals that Google's algorithms evaluate when determining search rankings. You optimize title tags and meta descriptions. You build backlinks from authoritative sites. You ensure your site loads quickly and works on mobile devices. You create content that targets specific keywords with appropriate density and placement. These tactics work because they align with how Google's systems assess page quality and relevance.</p> <p>AIO requires understanding how language models decide which sources to reference when answering questions. These models don't follow the same rules as search engine algorithms. They're not counting backlinks or analyzing page load speed. They're evaluating whether content provides clear, accurate, comprehensive answers to questions people actually ask. They're assessing credibility through different signals than traditional search engines use. They're making probabilistic decisions about which information best satisfies a query based on patterns learned during training and information retrieved during real-time web searches.</p> <p>The distinction matters because tactics that boost Google rankings don't automatically improve your chances of being cited by AI models, and vice versa. A page optimized perfectly for SEO might never appear in AI responses if it doesn't align with how language models evaluate content. Conversely, content that AI models consistently cite might not rank highly in traditional search if it lacks conventional SEO signals.</p> <p>This doesn't mean you should abandon SEO and focus exclusively on AIO. The two approaches are complementary, not competing. People still use Google extensively, and traditional search traffic remains valuable. The point is that comprehensive visibility requires optimizing for both channels. You need your content discoverable through conventional search engines and reliably cited by AI models. This dual approach captures traffic from users regardless of which discovery method they prefer.</p> <p>The strategic value of AIO extends beyond just additional traffic. When an AI model cites your content, it provides context explaining why your resource is valuable. The model doesn't just list your URL like a search result—it summarizes your key points, extracts relevant information, and positions your content as a trusted source. This creates a stronger credibility signal than a traditional search result because the AI has effectively pre-vetted your content and endorsed it as worth reading.</p> <p>Think about the user experience difference. In traditional search, someone sees your site listed among ten results and must decide whether to click based on a title and two-line description. In AI search, someone reads an answer that includes information from your content, sees your site cited as the source, and arrives at your page already understanding its value and relevance. The qualification happens before the click, resulting in higher-quality traffic with better engagement metrics.</p> <p>Google's introduction of AI Mode represents a pivotal moment in search engine evolution and confirms that AI-generated answers are becoming a core component of how major platforms deliver information. Understanding this development helps contextualize why AIO matters and where organic discovery is headed.</p> <p>AI Mode transforms Google's interface from a list of links into a conversational AI that provides direct answers. When you access AI Mode (available at google.com/ai or through the Google app), you interact with a language model that searches the web in real-time and synthesizes comprehensive responses to your questions. Instead of scanning through multiple websites, you receive curated information with sources cited, similar to ChatGPT with web search or Perplexity.</p> <p>What makes this particularly significant is Google's market position. Despite the rise of alternative AI search tools, Google still processes billions of searches daily and serves as the primary discovery mechanism for most internet users. When Google integrates AI-generated answers into its core search experience, it's not experimenting with a niche feature—it's fundamentally changing how the world's most popular search engine works.</p> <p>The financial implications validate this direction. Google reported that AI features contributed to a 10% increase in search revenue, reaching $50.7 billion in Q1 2025. This isn't a failing experiment that might be discontinued. It's a successful product innovation that's generating substantial revenue while improving user experience. Google has every incentive to expand AI Mode and integrate its capabilities more deeply into standard search.</p> <p>Currently, AI Mode exists as a separate interface that users must access intentionally, but the trajectory is clear. Google has indicated that AI-generated answers will eventually become a more prominent part of standard search results. While they've walked back statements about making AI Mode the default search experience after initial concerns, the long-term direction remains toward greater AI integration. Traditional search results won't disappear, but AI-generated summaries will occupy increasingly valuable real estate on search result pages.</p> <p>This evolution mirrors what happened with featured snippets and knowledge panels over the past decade. Google gradually introduced elements that answered questions directly on the search page rather than requiring clicks to external sites. AI Mode represents the next iteration of this trend—more comprehensive answers, synthesized from multiple sources, delivered conversationally rather than as extracted snippets.</p> <p>For content creators, this creates both opportunities and challenges. The opportunity is that appearing in AI-generated responses places your content in a prominent, trusted position that provides context and drives qualified traffic. The challenge is that optimization strategies must adapt to capture this visibility. Content that ranks well in traditional search results won't automatically appear in AI Mode responses without deliberate optimization for how AI systems evaluate and select sources.</p> <p>The global availability of AI Mode in over 180 countries means this isn't a gradual rollout that you can monitor and prepare for leisurely. It's happening now, and users worldwide are already accessing AI-powered search. Your competitors might be optimizing for these systems while you're still focused exclusively on traditional SEO, giving them an advantage in capturing traffic from this rapidly growing segment.</p> <p>One of the biggest challenges with AI Optimization is measurement. Traditional SEO provides robust analytics through Google Search Console, showing exactly which queries trigger impressions, how often people click your results, and where you rank for specific keywords. These metrics make it straightforward to track SEO progress and identify opportunities for improvement.</p> <p>AIO lacks this infrastructure. This creates a visibility problem—you can't optimize what you can't measure.</p> <p>Several commercial tools have emerged to fill this gap, offering AIO tracking and monitoring services. Keyword.com offers competitive pricing with various tier options.</p> <p>These tools work by systematically querying AI models with specific prompts and analyzing which sources appear in the responses. They help you understand whether your content shows up for relevant queries, how you compare to competitors, and how your visibility changes over time. This gap between professional tools and budget-conscious creators leaves many people flying blind with no way to measure their AIO performance.</p> <p>The solution is building your own tracking system using no-code automation tools. This approach requires more initial setup but provides ongoing monitoring at a fraction of commercial tool costs. The system I built uses Make.com, a no-code automation platform, to query AI models systematically, analyze responses, and track mentions over time. Make offers 1,000 operations monthly on their free tier, making it possible to start tracking without any monetary investment.</p> <p>The tracking system consists of three automated scenarios that work together to provide comprehensive AIO monitoring. The first scenario handles query tracking and brand mentions, automatically sending prompts to ChatGPT and recording which sources appear in responses. The second scenario performs keyword performance analysis, tracking specific topics or phrases relevant to your business and monitoring whether you're gaining or losing visibility. The third scenario focuses on competitor tracking, identifying when competitors appear in AI responses and analyzing their positioning compared to yours.</p> <p>Building this system requires understanding of Make.com's interface and basic automation concepts, but it's accessible to anyone willing to invest a few hours in setup. The difficulty level sits at intermediate—more complex than basic automation but far simpler than custom programming. Once configured, the system runs automatically on whatever schedule you set, collecting data and building a historical record of your AIO performance.</p> <p>The workflow begins with identifying the queries you want to track. These are essentially "AIO keywords"—questions that people might ask AI models where your content should ideally appear in the answer. Unlike traditional SEO keywords, which are often short phrases, AIO queries tend to be longer, more conversational questions that reflect how people actually talk to AI assistants.</p> <p>For example, instead of targeting the SEO keyword "WordPress hosting," you'd track the AIO query "What's the best WordPress hosting for SaaS applications?" or "Which hosting provider should I choose for a WordPress-based business site?" These natural language questions better represent how people interact with AI tools and help you optimize for actual usage patterns rather than keyword variations.</p> <p>Finding these queries requires a different research approach than traditional keyword research. This means thinking about their problems, concerns, and information needs, then formulating those as conversational queries. Tools like an LLM Query Generator can help by analyzing your content and suggesting relevant questions people might ask to find that information.</p> <p>Once you've identified target queries, the automated system tests them periodically—daily, weekly, or on whatever schedule makes sense for your monitoring needs. If you're appearing reliably for some questions but not others in the same category, you can analyze what makes your successful content different and apply those lessons to underperforming pieces. If your visibility is declining over time, you know you need to refresh and strengthen your content to maintain AI citation rates.</p> <p>This measurement foundation transforms AIO from guesswork into a data-driven practice. Instead of optimizing blindly and hoping AI models notice, you track actual performance and refine your approach based on concrete results. The initial investment in building or subscribing to tracking tools pays dividends through improved optimization efficiency and clearer understanding of what tactics actually work for your specific content and audience.</p> <p>Understanding AIO conceptually is valuable, but implementation requires specific, actionable tactics that demonstrably improve your chances of appearing in AI-generated responses. These seven strategies have proven effective across different content types, industries, and AI platforms. They work because they align with how language models evaluate sources and decide which content to cite when formulating answers.</p> <p>The first tactic centers on incorporating statistics, numbers, and verifiable proof throughout your content. AI models exhibit a strong preference for factual, data-backed information over general statements or opinions. When a model encounters two sources covering the same topic, one making vague claims and another providing specific numbers with citations, the statistical content almost always wins.</p> <p>This doesn't mean stuffing your content with random numbers. It means grounding your claims in specific, verifiable data wherever possible. Instead of writing "Our tool is widely used," you'd write "Our tool has 150,000 monthly active users with a 4.7 out of 5 satisfaction rating based on 3,200 reviews." The specificity signals credibility to AI models, which learned during training that precise data indicates reliable sources.</p> <p>The same principle applies to any factual claim. When discussing market trends, cite specific growth percentages and time periods. When mentioning company performance, include actual revenue figures or user counts. When describing product features, provide concrete specifications rather than abstract descriptions. Each piece of specific data you add increases the likelihood that AI models will view your content as authoritative and citation-worthy.</p> <p>This approach requires sourcing and maintaining accurate information, which means you can't fabricate numbers or exaggerate metrics. AI models increasingly cross-reference claims across sources, and inconsistencies damage credibility. The data you include must be truthful and, where relevant, attributed to primary sources. But when you consistently provide specific, accurate information, you build a reputation as a reliable source that AI models return to repeatedly.</p> <p>The second tactic involves active engagement on Reddit, Quora, and similar community forums. This strategy works for a less obvious reason than you might expect. It's not primarily about direct traffic from forum posts, though that can be valuable. It's about creating authentic mentions and discussions of your content across platforms that AI models frequently encounter during training and web searches.</p> <p>Language models learn from vast datasets that include substantial amounts of community discussion content. Reddit threads, Quora answers, and forum posts represent genuine human conversations about real topics, making them high-value training data. When your content or expertise appears naturally in these discussions, it creates signals that AI models recognize and incorporate into their understanding of what resources exist and who's knowledgeable about specific topics.</p> <p>The key word here is "naturally." AI models have learned to recognize and discount obvious spam, self-promotion, and link-dropping. Simply posting your URL in relevant threads won't help and might actually hurt if it generates negative reactions or gets flagged as spam. Instead, you need to participate genuinely in communities where your expertise is relevant, providing real value in discussions and mentioning your content only when it truly addresses someone's question or adds to the conversation.</p> <p>This means answering questions thoroughly, sharing insights from your experience, helping solve problems, and building a reputation as a knowledgeable contributor before you ever share links. When you do reference your content, it should be in the context of "I wrote a detailed guide about exactly this problem that covers X, Y, and Z" rather than "Check out my site." The former contributes to the discussion while the latter feels promotional.</p> <p>Over time, this authentic participation creates a distributed network of references to your expertise and content across platforms that AI models access. These organic mentions, especially when they're accompanied by positive community response, signal that you're a legitimate authority worth citing. The impact accumulates gradually but compounds over months as you build a presence in relevant communities.</p> <p>The third tactic focuses on optimizing for natural language queries rather than keyword stuffing. Traditional SEO often encourages optimizing for specific keyword phrases, sometimes at the expense of natural writing. You might structure sentences awkwardly to include exact keyword matches or repeat phrases more often than sounds natural. This approach can work for search engines that match keywords mechanically.</p> <p>AI models process language differently. They understand semantic meaning and context, not just keyword matching. When people query AI tools, they ask complete questions in conversational language: "What's the best WordPress hosting for SaaS applications?" rather than "WordPress hosting SaaS." Your content needs to answer these natural questions directly and comprehensively to appear in AI responses.</p> <p>This means structuring your content around questions your audience actually asks. Include FAQ sections that address common queries in full-sentence question format. Write subheadings as questions rather than just topics. Provide complete answers that someone could understand without additional context. Make your content readable and helpful to humans first, trusting that AI models will recognize and value that quality.</p> <p>The practical implementation involves thinking about the conversation your audience wants to have rather than the keywords they might type. What are they trying to accomplish? What confuses them? What decisions are they facing? What objections or concerns do they have? When you address these elements in natural, conversational language, you simultaneously create content that people find valuable and that AI models recognize as comprehensive answers to common questions.</p> <p>The fourth tactic requires creating comparison tables and structured data that AI models can easily parse and reference. Language models excel at processing structured information organized in clear, consistent formats. When they encounter well-formatted comparison tables, step-by-step lists, or data organized in predictable structures, they can extract and cite that information more reliably than when similar content appears in dense paragraphs.</p> <p>This doesn't mean every piece of content should become a table or list. It means that when you're presenting information that naturally fits structured formats—comparisons between options, sequential steps in a process, multiple examples of a concept, sets of tips or recommendations—you should use formatting that makes that structure explicit and easy to process.</p> <p>For example, if you're comparing different software tools, create an actual comparison table with columns for features, pricing, pros, and cons rather than describing each tool in paragraph form. If you're explaining a multi-step process, number the steps and use consistent formatting for each. If you're providing examples, use a predictable structure where each example follows the same pattern.</p> <p>The benefit extends beyond AI optimization. Structured content is easier for human readers to scan and comprehend too. People increasingly skim content rather than reading every word, and clear structure helps them extract key information quickly. When you optimize for both AI processing and human scanning through better structure, you improve the experience for all visitors while increasing AI citation rates.</p> <p>Implementation requires evaluating your existing content and identifying opportunities to add structure without forcing it artificially. Look for places where you're listing multiple items in prose that would be clearer as bullet points. Find sections comparing options that would benefit from table format. Identify processes that could be broken into numbered steps. These changes often improve content quality while making it more AI-friendly.</p> <p>The fifth tactic involves building multi-platform authority by publishing consistent information across different channels. AI models, particularly those with web search capabilities, often cross-reference information across sources to verify accuracy and assess credibility. When they find the same core information presented consistently on your website, in your social media content, in articles you've published elsewhere, and in your responses on community platforms, it signals that you're a legitimate authority on that topic.</p> <p>This doesn't mean duplicating content identically across platforms, which could create SEO problems and doesn't align with best practices for different mediums. It means maintaining consistent expertise, perspectives, and factual information while adapting the format and style to each platform's norms and audience expectations.</p> <p>Your core message and expertise should be recognizable across a blog post on your website, a LinkedIn article, a Twitter thread, a YouTube video description, and a guest post on another site. This consistency reinforces your authority and makes it easier for AI models to identify you as a reliable source on specific topics.</p> <p>Building this multi-platform presence takes time and consistent effort. Early on, you might only appear in AI responses when the model happens to encounter your website. As you build presence across platforms, the model has multiple opportunities to encounter your expertise from different angles, increasing the likelihood that it recognizes you as an authority worth citing.</p> <p>The sixth tactic emphasizes showing fresh update signals throughout your content. AI models, especially those with real-time web access, demonstrate preference for current information over dated content. The opportunity is that regularly updating content can improve AI citation rates even if the core information hasn't changed dramatically. This simple addition can significantly impact whether AI models view your content as relevant for queries about current state or recent developments.</p> <p>Beyond update dates, freshness signals include referencing recent events, citing current statistics and data, mentioning the current year in context where relevant, and updating examples to reflect current tools and practices. These signals reassure both AI models and human readers that the information hasn't become outdated even if the core topic is relatively stable.</p> <p>The practical challenge is balancing the benefit of updates against the time investment required. Content about rapidly changing topics needs more frequent updates than evergreen material. During these reviews, update statistics, add recent examples, remove dated references, and add the new update date. This structured approach ensures your most important content remains fresh without requiring constant attention to every article.</p> <p>The seventh tactic involves implementing JSON-LD structured data markup on your web pages. This technical optimization helps AI models understand your content's structure and purpose by providing machine-readable information about what your page contains, what type of content it is, and how different elements relate to each other.</p> <p>Structured data uses a standardized format called Schema.org vocabulary implemented through JSON-LD script tags. These tags don't affect how your content appears to human visitors, but they provide clear signals to automated systems parsing your pages, including AI models determining whether your content answers specific queries.</p> <p>Common structured data types relevant for most content include Article (marking blog posts and articles), HowTo (for step-by-step guides), FAQ (for question-and-answer sections), Person (for author bios), Organization (for company information), and Product (for product pages). Implementing appropriate schema markup for your content type helps AI models categorize and understand your content more accurately.</p> <p>The technical implementation requires adding JSON-LD scripts to your page HTML, typically in the header section.
