Clinical Challenge: Cough, Fever, in Person Who Vapes</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.psychiatryadvisor.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/8/2022/01/smokingvapingteenagerg51500842_1324038.jpg" alt="Clinical Challenge: Cough, Fever, in Person Who Vapes" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>A 16-year-old adolescent presents to the emergency department with a 3-day history of vomiting, tactile fevers, and a mild headache that went away 2 days earlier. The patient denies any abdominal or flank pain, dysuria, diarrhea, or other complaints. When specifically questioned, she acknowledges a slight cough but has no shortness of breath or chest pain.</p> <p>The patient’s vital signs are normal except for an elevated temperature (100.3 °F) and a pulse rate 133 beats per minute. Initial physical examination is otherwise normal with no rash, tonsillar exudate, rales, murmur, flank tenderness, or other abnormality. Chest radiographs (Figure 1-2) and blood work are ordered. Laboratory results are within normal range except for an elevated white blood cell count (19,000/μL). Pregnancy and COVID-19 PCR tests are negative.</p> <p>Can you diagnose this condition? What is the most important medical history question to ask?</p> <p>This article originally appeared on Clinical Advisor</p> <p>Psychiatry Advisor, a trusted source of medical news and feature content for healthcare providers, offers clinicians insight into the latest research to inform clinical practice and improve patient outcomes.</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.psychiatryadvisor.com/home/topics/addiction/tobacco-use-disorder/clinical-challenge-cough-fever-person-who-vapes/" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9617"> <h2>#9617. The Simple Drink Swap Linked To 41% More Weight Loss</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.spring.org.uk/images/drink-water-1.jpg" alt="The Simple Drink Swap Linked To 41% More Weight Loss" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>Women who changed their usual lunchtime drink lost 41 per cent more weight over 18 months. What made the difference?</p> <p>Women who changed their usual lunchtime drink lost 41 per cent more weight over 18 months. What made the difference?</p> <p>Swapping diet drinks for water could help people lose more weight.</p> <p>Women with type 2 diabetes who make the switch lose around 41 percent more weight over 18 months than those who continue drinking diet beverages.</p> <p>They are also twice as likely to achieve diabetes remission during a structured weight-management programme.</p> <p>The findings raise a question about whether a drink’s calorie count tells the whole story about its effects on weight.</p> <p>Sweet taste without the accompanying energy might influence appetite signals.</p> <p>The results suggest that everyday drink choices could play a useful supporting role in longer-term weight management.</p> <p>The research involved around 80 women who were overweight or had obesity, had type 2 diabetes and regularly consumed diet drinks.</p> <p>Researchers randomly assigned them either to replace their usual diet beverage with water after lunch five times a week or to continue drinking it.</p> <p>Both groups took part in a six-month weight-loss programme followed by a year devoted to maintaining their progress.</p> <p>By the end, women assigned to water had lost an average of 6.82 kg, compared with 4.85 kg among those continuing with diet drinks.</p> <p>The difference amounted to almost 2 kg of additional weight loss across the programme.</p> <p>The water group also showed greater improvements in measures including fasting blood glucose, insulin resistance and blood fats.</p> <p>Diabetes remission was reported in 90 percent of women assigned to water, compared with 45 percent of those continuing diet beverages.</p> <p>Dr Hamid R. Farshchi, study co-author, said:</p> <p>“It’s a small change with the potential for a big impact on long-term health outcomes.”</p> <p>The brain may respond differently when a sweet taste arrives without the energy normally supplied by sugar.</p> <p>In a separate experiment involving around 75 adults, participants reported greater hunger after consuming sucralose than sugar, and the sweetener altered activity in the hypothalamus, a brain region involved in appetite regulation (Chakravartti et al., 2025).</p> <p>However, hunger ratings after sucralose did not differ from those after water, so the findings do not establish that sweetened drinks necessarily make people hungrier than plain water.</p> <p>The mismatch between sweetness and energy might help explain some appetite responses, but whether it contributed to the weight-loss difference remains unknown.</p> <p>The study was published in the journal Diabetes (Farshchi Nasr et al., 2025).</p> <p>Psychologist, Jeremy Dean, PhD is the founder and author of PsyBlog. He holds a doctorate in psychology from University College London and two other advanced degrees in psychology. He has been writing about scientific research on PsyBlog since 2004. View all posts by Dr Jeremy Dean</p> <p>Join the free PsyBlog mailing list. Apple Streusel Meal Prep Muffins</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://pinchofyum.com/tachyon/Apple-Streusel-Muffins-scaled.jpg" alt="Apple Streusel Meal Prep Muffins" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>Super wholesome, loaded with streusel, and ideal for meal prep! My kids love them!</p> <p>Published by Lindsay Ostrom on October 9, 2026</p> <p>YUM these little meal prep apple muffins have been such a treat for my mornings!</p> <p>Open windows! Crisp fall air! Hot coffee! A warm, streusely, lightly cinnamony apple muffin with tons of wholesome stuff in it and a generous pat of butter on top! It’s what I’m doing every day right now, and it’s my dream life.</p> <p>The main ingredients here are shockingly basic:</p> <p>I threw some brown sugar streusel on top, because streusel increases my interest in any muffin by about 500%.</p> <p>I’ve been packing one of these in my girls’ lunchboxes almost every time we pack a cold lunch! I also bring them for a car snack after school pick up. My kids honestly eat one of these (or these pumpkin ones, or these zucchini ones) once a day at this point.</p> <p>I don’t know that anyone cares about this, but I spend too much time thinking about these things.</p> <p>5 Stars 4 Stars 3 Stars 2 Stars 1 Star</p> <p>These apple streusel meal prep muffins are super wholesome, loaded with streusel, and ideal for prepping ahead! My kids love them!</p> <p>Keywords: apple muffins, apple streusel muffins, meal prep muffins</p> <p>I love hearing from you! Leave a comment or rating below!</p> <p>I’m Lindsay and I ♡ FOOD. I used to be a teacher, and now making food and writing about it online is my full-time job. I love talking with people about food, and I'm so glad you're here.</p> <p>Did you make a recipe? Tag @pinchofyum on Instagram so we can find you!</p> <p>Your email address will not be published. Required fields are marked *</p> <p>Sign me up for recipes, please!All the food, right to your inbox (and a FREE ecookbook, too!).</p> <p>I made these following the directions. Nobody liked them. First, my vitamix struggled to blend all of those layered ingredients. I had to remove some and blend in batches. Second, the texture and flavor were not great. I have enjoyed all your other recipes that I’ve made, but this bombed. Me and the waiting grandkids were disappointed.</p> <p>Oh yum! My son and I just made these and they are SO good! The house smells amazing! These are such a great snack on a rainy, dark fall afternoon after school. Thank you! Please keep the goodness coming! 🙂</p> <p>Love to hear that you and your son cooked baked together!</p> <p>Looking for some help. Mine came out really dense and kind of gummy. Maybe I over blended? Still yummy and I’ll try to make again and troubleshoot</p> <p>This can happen with baked goods that only use oats. Did you let the batter sit out for a while? Baking the batter right away can sometimes help.</p> <p>As expected given all your other great recipes, these were DELICIOUS and the whole family loved them! My intention was to freeze some but I don’t think they will last that long at my house. Will definitely make again!</p> <p>My vitamix didn’t do a great job blending when I started with oats at the bottom. I’ll add the liquid ingredients first next time.</p> <p>oh, that’s a good note – for the liquids to go first!</p> <p>Just ordered the FULLSTAR chopper! Thanks for the recommendation. So much faster to get dinner ready. Smooch!~!</p> <p>Easy and delicious! I made them with my toddler and we gobbled them up. I lowered the sugar to 1/2c and baked the extra batter into mini muffins that cooked in 12 minutes 🙂</p> <p>These are SO GOOD and soooo nice and easy cause of blending everything. I used coconut sugar instead of brown, and gala apples instead of honeycrisp cause it’s what I had on hand, and they turned out amazing. Definitely going on the repeat list!</p> <p>Thank you for yet another amazing POY recipe!! Absolutely delicious!Followed the recipe almost exactly, except I had to sub 0% Greek Yogurt for the whole milk version as that’s all I have. I ate two in a row straight out of the oven, so yummy. Can’t wait to have one with my coffee in the morning and the rest will go in the freezer for a perfect breakfast-on-the-go for my daughter who has an hour bus ride to college very early. I’ve made so many POY recipes now (made the Apple Crisp for dessert today too) they never fail, are always delicious and the whole family (fussy husband, two teens, a tween…and occasionally a 5yr old Labrador) love them.</p> <p>I don’t have a Vitamix but this definitely didn’t work in my super basic blender! I ended up using my food processor with the oats first, then adding everything after. That worked great!</p> <p>Oh, thank you for the notes on using the food processor! I know others were interested in using it.</p> <p>Delightful little fall recipe! Not too sweet, was great w my coffee this morning. I used what apples I had on hand (gala)= 2.5 small ones. My cupcake pan holds 12, so I used my mini pan w/ the extra batter and got 16 minis too. (Cooked those for about 12 minutes along with the big ones).</p> <p>I would make these again. It was a little putzsy as I only have a mini blender, so I had to blend in batches.</p> <p>I swapped the oats for oat flour I already had and didn’t check my ratio so it made a few more muffins (3.5 cups oats = roughly 2.67 cups oat flour). Also added about .5 cup of oats to the topping to get an apple crisp topping.</p> <p>Would love to know why you don’t recommend the Costco sprouted oats, that’s almost all we use. Love all your recipes and look forward to trying this!</p> <p>Lauren, I just wanted to let you know my family made these with the Costco sprouted oats because that’s what we had on hand and we were impatient. My family still loved them and they were worth making. I’m guessing they would have been a little softer with old-fashioned rolled oats because they were maybe slightly tough, BUT it really wasn’t an issue for us.</p> <p>I have applesauce on hand instead of fresh apples, would that work as a substitute?</p> <p>Also curious about applesauce, if it’s getting blended already!</p> <p>These are delicious! I didn’t have a full cup of Greek yogurt so I added some cottage cheese and sour cream to make 1 cup. Otherwise followed the recipe as written. Supper easy to make and everyone loved them. Will definitely make these again.</p> <p>These look delicious! Can you use sour cream instead of greek yoghurt?</p> <p>Could you use food processor instead of blender? Excited to try this!</p> <p>I used a food processor and they came out great!</p> <p>These sound delicious. You mentioned that you used brown sugar instead of maple syrup for this recipe. If I preferred to use maple syrup, what would be the recommended amount?</p> <p>I haven’t tried it – I just went straight for the brown sugar to save some dollars. 🙂 And the flavor is delicious. But I would like to try it, just so we know how it works with maple syrup. I will report back when I do! (I have several muffins in this same style and they use between 1/2 cup and 3/4 cup maple syrup, but I don’t want to confirm that for this one until I know for sure.)</p> <p>Lindsay said in the article that the Costco sprouted oats aren’t recommended because they absorb liquid a different way. She also said quick oats do as well and that’s why they’re not recommended either.</p> <p>I'm a former 4th grade teacher, now full time blogger. My husband Bjork and I live in Minnesota. Fall Freezer Meals #2</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://pinchofyum.com/tachyon/Fall-Freezer-Meals-2-1.jpg" alt="Fall Freezer Meals #2" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>These Fall Freezer Meals have been SO helpful for us. The prep is shockingly easy!</p> <p>Published by Lindsay Ostrom on October 14, 2026</p> <p>A few months ago, I discovered what feels like a little life hack.</p> <p>I started spending an hour each month getting a few meals prepped for the month ahead. We’re talking just assembling stuff for my favorite recipes into bags and freezing it!</p> <p>And I can’t tell you how much this system makes me feel like I have my life together! It’s the best.</p> <p>The recipes this month are absolute family favorites for fall!</p> <p>And they all have cook times for Crockpot, Instant Pot, and stovetop methods. 🙂</p> <p>Hope these help make your life easier this month like they have for us!</p> <p>Everything you need is right on them. I print the cards out and attach them to the bags so I don’t have to use my phone at all for the prep or cooking.</p> <p>For the streusel: mix 4 tablespoons melted butter, 1/3 cup brown sugar, and 3/4 cup flour into small crumbles.</p> <p>Spray a muffin tin with avocado oil. Fill tins two-thirds of the way full with batter; top with streusel.</p> <p>Store muffins in an airtight container or bag in the freezer (or fridge). To reheat from frozen, microwave 45-60 seconds.</p> <p>Remove chicken from the sauce and shred. Blend sauce until smooth. Add chicken back in. Serve in tortillas with all the taco fixings you want!</p> <p>Add 1-2 cups heavy cream and 1-2 cups chicken broth (as needed). To thicken: whisk 2 tbsp. cornstarch with 2 tbsp. cold water; add and simmer.</p> <p>Whisk 1 1/2 tbsp. cornstarch in 1 1/2 tbsp. cold water; add to bubbling pot and let simmer until slightly thickened.</p> <p>Stir in 2 cups of fresh spinach and fresh cilantro just before serving.</p> <p>Serve with rice and chili crisp. I also love this with cucumber salad (thinly sliced cucumber and red onion, tossed with vinegar, avocado oil, salt, and sugar).</p> <p>I’m Lindsay and I ♡ FOOD. I used to be a teacher, and now making food and writing about it online is my full-time job. I love talking with people about food, and I'm so glad you're here.</p> <p>Did you make a recipe? Tag @pinchofyum on Instagram so we can find you!</p> <p>Your email address will not be published. Required fields are marked *</p> <p>Sign me up for recipes, please!All the food, right to your inbox (and a FREE ecookbook, too!).</p> <p>I love this idea! Spending just an hour preparing freezer meals for the month sounds like such a practical way to make busy weekdays easier. The variety is great too, especially having options like chicken tinga tacos, wild rice soup, and chickpea curry with different cooking methods. I also appreciate the printable labels and grocery lists because they make meal prep much more organized. These recipes would be especially helpful for anyone balancing a busy schedule with home-cooked meals. Thanks for sharing!</p> <p>Very interesting post. Just thinking about the option to add to instant pot. How would that work? You put everything frozen (without any other unfrozen liquid), put the lid and select the number of minutes? So everything will thaw in the IP before it pressurized?</p> <p>Hi there, how long do these recipes stay good for in the freezer? I would like to have these as back ups. Thank you.</p> <p>Love your recipes! I love curry and the recipe for Chickpea curry looks fabulous, but, my husband is not a chickpea for protein kind of guy. Can I use chicken or shrimp instead and how much would I use?</p> <p>Can you clarify the liquid added to the chicken and wild rice soup? I’m reading 5 cups broth for cooking and then another 2.5 to finish with 2 cups cream, is that right?</p> <p>Hello! Yes, it is another 1-2 cups of broth added, as needed, with the cream. You can adjust depending on how thick you like your soup.</p> <p>Thank you so much for sharing these wonderful ideas! I love your recipes. For the Chicken Wild Rice Soup- Would a combination of Heavy Cream and Whole Milk work here like in the original blog post? What ratio do you think would be best if I did that? Thank you!</p> <p>I love both the original bechamel (butter / flour / milk) method, and the heavy cream method! 🙂 For this version, I opted for the heavy cream just because it’s easier to put onto the small cards. But the bechamel is great and it will get a bit thicker than just using cream. If you want that version, I’d just make the bechamel and add it at the end, using the same quantities as in this post: https://pinchofyum.com/crockpot-chicken-wild-rice-soup</p> <p>Hi there! Always wondering about the prep for chicken thighs, how much do you trim the fat and gristle from them? It takes me so long and I’m always wondering if it’s worth doing.</p> <p>Unless it’s a big piece of fat that you can easily cut off, you can definitely skip the trimming.</p> <p>Love the recipes I have tried! Going to try the freezer prep soup and muffins. Thanks for the recipes</p> <p>Can you use chicken breast instead of chicken thighs in the tinga tacos?</p> <p>Yep! I prefer thighs because they stay a bit juicier, but chicken breasts can absolutely work. 🙂 I would pull them out of the sauce when they’re done and really kind of -chop them into shreddy chunks rather than straight shred them – maybe it’s just me, but I find that sometimes the shredding with chicken breasts can get a bit stringy.</p> <p>Hi Lindsay, Thank you so much for all of your great recipes and ideas! I really appreciate all the hard work.</p> <p>You’re so welcome! I really have enjoyed doing these for myself these last few months, so it’s fun to share them!</p> <p>Lindsay – LOVE your recipes! Question about the freezer meals. There are a couple that you say you freeze the chicken separately but on the Chicken Wild Rice Soup it looks like you put the chicken in the same bag with everything. Can you please clarify for me? Thank you!!</p> <p>Yes! 🙂 Short answer – you can put the chicken in the bag, or add it later. Either can work. Long answer – With the first batch I did in September, I left the chicken out and added it at the time of cooking (and I wrote that into those recipe cards). I liked how it cooked, but I found it was a little bit inconvenient because I didn’t always have chicken on hand when I needed it. So for round two / the set of recipes in this post, I decided to include the chicken in the bag. All these recipes now have chicken going into the bag with everything else, and all the cook times are listed with that in mind.</p> <p>These were so easy and awesome. I prepped one of everything for my friend who just had a major surgery, and another batch for my family. I hope you keep coming out with these!</p> <p>Love that you are sharing these meals with others!</p> <p>Any replacement ideas for chipotles in adobo? Worried too spicy for the kids.</p> <p>Freezer crockpot meals are great for camping. Prep is pretty much done. Put them in the crockpot and enjoy after a day of hiking and fun. Delicious!</p> <p>I’ve been freezer cooking for years and have seen nearly all the websites on the topic.</p> <p>Yours are simply THE BEST label layout I’ve ever come across! Kudos to you!</p> <p>Thank you so much Jerri! I work on these freezer meals with Jenna on our team, and the two of us really try to make them feel as user friendly as possible! 🙂</p> <p>I'm a former 4th grade teacher, now full time blogger. Sloppy Joe’s with Ranch Potatoes</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://pinchofyum.com/tachyon/Sloppy-Joes_HighRes-014-scaled.jpg" alt="Sloppy Joe’s with Ranch Potatoes" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>Easy, saucy, delicious Sloppy Joe’s! My kids’ favorite dinner. Super simple to make with just a few ingredients.</p> <p>Published by Lindsay Ostrom on October 28, 2026</p> <p>Here’s the thing – it’s humble, it’s non-fancy, but my husband and my kids are so happy when I make this for dinner.</p> <p>I’ve been on a JOURNEY with these. I tried making Sloppy Joe’s several ways this summer, since my daughter kept asking for them. But with every batch I made, she always kindly let me know that they were still “not as good as the ones at school.”</p> <p>Lucky for me (and all of us), I know several of the wonderful people who do the food service at their school. I was able to get some school recipe intel, which is how I ended up with this very simple “recipe”:</p> <p>It’s rich, and meaty, and easy, and just so very family-friendly.</p> <p>Bjork and I like ours topped with pickled jalapenos or crispy onions, and the girls, of course, like them “plain” on a squishy white bun.</p> <p>I always always make these with what we call Ranch Potatoes, which are the truly the delight of my life. In our house, it’s not Sloppy Joe’s if there’s no pile of crispy, buttery Ranch Potatoes on the side. 🙂</p> <p>Regarding diced onion, pepper, or garlic in the Sloppy Joe filling: this recipe has none. Everyone I cook for enjoys these the same (or even more?) with an uncluttered texture and just a few hits of garlic and onion powder instead, which makes this whole thing even faster and easier.</p> <p>My youngest requested this as her birthday meal this year. Hope you like it as much as we do!</p> <p>Leave it sitting undisturbed for a few minutes so that it develops a nice golden crust.</p> <p>Garlic powder, onion powder, beef bouillon, ketchup, and BBQ sauce!</p> <p>Add some water as needed to make the mixture loosen up and turn a bit glossy. It can just hang out until you’re ready to eat.</p> <p>When you’re close to eating, pop your potatoes in the oven.</p> <p>Once they’re roasty toasty, add a knob of butter and some ranch seasoning. Toss to combine. (If you don’t have ranch seasoning, just use melted butter, fresh garlic, and dill. UNREAL.)</p> <p>Load it onto a soft bun – we love this with ranch potatoes and green beans!</p> <p>5 Stars 4 Stars 3 Stars 2 Stars 1 Star</p> <p>Easy, saucy, delicious Sloppy Joe’s! My kids’ favorite dinner. We love these with Ranch Potatoes!</p> <p>White garlic sauce (for dipping, as shown in the video): Whisk 1/4 cup mayo, 1/4 cup plain Greek yogurt, 1 clove grated garlic, 1-2 tablespoons water, and salt to taste.</p> <p>Making Ahead: The meat mixture is ready to go right after you add the ketchup and BBQ sauce, but I usually like to let it simmer for 30-60 minutes to really caramelize around the edges and deepen in both flavor and color. It also works perfectly to keep it warm in the crockpot after cooking!</p> <p>Keywords: sloppy joe’s, sloppy joe sandwiches, easy dinner, kid-friendly dinner</p> <p>I love hearing from you! Leave a comment or rating below!</p> <p>I’m Lindsay and I ♡ FOOD. I used to be a teacher, and now making food and writing about it online is my full-time job. I love talking with people about food, and I'm so glad you're here.</p> <p>Did you make a recipe? Tag @pinchofyum on Instagram so we can find you!</p> <p>Your email address will not be published. Required fields are marked *</p> <p>Sign me up for recipes, please!All the food, right to your inbox (and a FREE ecookbook, too!).</p> <p>I thought I had a favorite sloppy Joe recipe…until I made these! They’re so, so delicious, and so easy to make! And the ranch potatoes were the perfect side. These are going in my regular rotation!</p> <p>The school-cafeteria intel made me laugh — kids comparing home cooking to the school lunch is universal; here in Japan, school lunch (kyushoku) sets the same impossibly high bar. I love that the winning recipe turned out to be this simple: bouillon base, ketchup, and BBQ sauce. The ranch potatoes are happening at my house this week.</p> <p>This was absolutely delicious. I need to add this to my regular rotation. Huge hit with the family!</p> <p>This was a hit with my family. The ranch potatoes are such a smart side with the sloppy joes. I will make this again soon.</p> <p>The sloppy Joes were delicious and easy! I love the idea of adding beef bullion. It definitely made it taste richer. I bought a jar of that for this recipe, along with the gorgeous brioche buns, at Costco. Be prepared to add a little more water at the end. I needed to add more to make it glossy and less sticky. This will be in our regular rotation!</p> <p>Yay – glad you loved in April! I agree about the water, I’m going to update that amount. I often need a bit more as well!</p> <p>My children all ate two helpings. This never happens. And those ranch potatoes are life changing.</p> <p>Amazing! It’s the best feeling! Thanks Lauren! 🙂 🙂</p> <p>This is a simple but delicious and nostalgic recipe. I made this last night and it was a hit.</p> <p>Do you have a favorite BBQ sauce for this recipe? I’m a vegetarian so can’t taste the recipe for my family – would love a recommendation!</p> <p>I’ve used the Trader Joe’s BBQ sauce for the last few batches and I really like it! 🙂</p> <p>Hi Linda! I have used a few kinds! Most frequent ones I’ve used are Trader Joe’s Kansas City BBQ sauce, or Famous Dave’s! 🙂</p> <p>This is such a throwback to the delicious sloppy joes of my childhood, I can already taste them! I’m a vegetarian now- any suggestion of what could be used in place of the meat? Wondering if a combo of beans and mushrooms might work…. off to do some research…. 🙂</p> <p>Hi Gigi: we are also mostly vegetarian (no red meat) so I make tofu crumbles. You can find a recipe on the internet. I freeze my tofu, thaw and drain it and then shred it on the large holes of a grater. Mix with seasonings and bake in the oven. I make a big batch and then seperate them into portions and freeze. Use them for this and anything else calling for ground beef. Hope this helps.</p> <p>Thanks for this! how would you adjust this if you wanted to create this and prep ahead of time, and serve later the next day in a crockpot?</p> <p>Jumping in to add that I also frequently 1.5x or 2x this and freeze whatever we don’t eat, since it works so well as a make-ahead! Especially when I know I’m going to be hosting or serving a crowd. Then I just reheat with a bit more water and sauce or warm in the crockpot.</p> <p>Make as is, then just put on low in a crockpot to rewarm!</p> <p>Ahhhhh Sloppy Joe’s!! My kids are now in their mid-20’s and these are STILL a family favorite haha. I love making them a nostalgic meal when they’re home. Can’t wait to try your version with the beef bouillon base…sounds like a perfect addition!</p> <p>It’s so funny, I make all of this (what I think is) interesting, fun, delicious food, but then I make just regular ol Sloppy Joe’s and my family is just swooning. 🙂 Hope my kids still want me to make these for them when they’re 20!</p> <p>I'm a former 4th grade teacher, now full time blogger. Does β‑Blocker Use Increase Depression Risk?</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.psychiatryadvisor.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/8/2022/01/pillsg730138337_1448007-e1656645198731.jpg" alt="Does β‑Blocker Use Increase Depression Risk?" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>The association between β-blocker use and depression was investigated in a population-based observational study recently published in the journal Drug Safety.</p> <p>While depression is often cited as an adverse effect of β-blocker use, there is limited evidence supporting this causal relationship. To better understand the association between beta blockers and the risk of new-onset depression, the study authors analyzed data from the UK population-based Clinical Practice Research Datalink (CPRD) GOLD database.</p> <p>“We identifed patients aged 18-80 years with an incident depression diagnosis between 2000 and 2016, and matched controls, and estimated the risk (odds ratio [OR]) of depression in association with use of β-blockers,” the study authors explained.</p> <p>Findings of the analysis revealed an increased risk of developing depression among short-term users of β-blockers compared with no use at all (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 1.91; 95% CI, 1.72-2.12).</p> <p>Among short-term users, increased risk of depression was mainly restricted to patients with a neuropsychiatric disorder taking propranolol (aOR 6.33, 95% CI 5.16–7.76).  Patients on propranolol for a cardiovascular indication were found to be at slightly elevated risk of depression (aOR 1.44, 95% CI 1.14–1.82). Apart from propranolol, no other lipophilic β-blocker or hydrophilic β-blocker was found to increase the risk of depression.</p> <p>Additionally, no association was observed between long-term use of β-blockers and the risk of depression (aOR, 0.85; 95% CI, 0.85-0.94).</p> <p>“Our findings suggest that the reported association between use of β-blockers and depression may not be causal but rather a result of protopathic bias,” the study authors concluded.</p> <p>Bornand D, Reinau D, Jick SS, Meier CR. β‑blockers and the risk of depression: A matched case–control study. Drug Safety. Published online January 19, 2022. https://doi.org/10.1007/s40264-021-01140-5.</p> <p>Psychiatry Advisor, a trusted source of medical news and feature content for healthcare providers, offers clinicians insight into the latest research to inform clinical practice and improve patient outcomes.</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.psychiatryadvisor.com/home/topics/mood-disorders/depressive-disorder/does-%ce%b2%e2%80%91blocker-use-increase-depression-risk/" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9608"> <h2>#9608. What Couples Married For 40 Years Do When Life Gets Hard</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.spring.org.uk/images/senior_couple.jpg" alt="What Couples Married For 40 Years Do When Life Gets Hard" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>Couples married for decades reveal what they turned to when they thought their marriage might end.</p> <p>Couples married for decades reveal what they turned to when they thought their marriage might end.</p> <p>When people in decades-long marriages describe what helped them through a crisis, most of the responses they give involve leaning on each other.</p> <p>They describe listening to each other, talking through painful subjects and sometimes having the same argument more than once.</p> <p>The researchers suggest that this response grows out of years of knowing they can count on their partner.</p> <p>In attachment theory, a partner can act as a safe haven, someone whose presence makes it easier to bear distress.</p> <p>Getting through a difficult period together may deepen that trust, making it easier to ask for help the next time it is needed.</p> <p>Dr Christian Heim, the study’s first author, and Dr Caroline Heim, study co-author, interviewed each couple together, asking each person to describe what had put their marriage under strain and what had helped them cope.</p> <p>The 180 participants were born in 24 countries and, with a few exceptions, had been married for at least 40 years.</p> <p>Around two-thirds of the couples described a threat they believed could have ended their marriage, such as the death or serious illness of a child, infidelity or prolonged periods apart.</p> <p>Talking, listening and arguing accounted for almost a quarter of the coping responses the researchers recorded.</p> <p>After an affair, some couples described arguing over it repeatedly, while bereaved partners sometimes waited for a moment when both felt able to speak.</p> <p>One partner in an American couple married for 45 years recalled asking their spouse about the son they had lost.</p> <p>“Can I talk about our son? I’m hurting. Is it okay to talk about it?”</p> <p>Some partners described taking time to grieve separately before they were ready to turn to each other.</p> <p>Around four in five coping responses involved leaning on the relationship, whether by drawing closer, persevering as a couple or giving up something one partner wanted.</p> <p>The interviews capture what couples in lasting marriages felt had helped them, leaving open whether the same approaches would have helped couples who separated.</p> <p>When partners see a problem as something they face together, they may spend less time working out who is to blame and more time trying to understand what the other person is going through.</p> <p>A previous analysis involving almost 18,000 people found that coping together and helping a partner manage stress were both linked to greater relationship satisfaction (Falconier et al., 2015).</p> <p>Some couples in the interviews felt that an illness, a bereavement or a family conflict had left them closer, even though the experience itself had been painful.</p> <p>A British couple married for 60 years described how they got through a serious conflict with their in-laws:</p> <p>The study was published in the journal The American Journal of Family Therapy (Heim & Heim, 2025).</p> <p>Psychologist, Jeremy Dean, PhD is the founder and author of PsyBlog. He holds a doctorate in psychology from University College London and two other advanced degrees in psychology. He has been writing about scientific research on PsyBlog since 2004. View all posts by Dr Jeremy Dean</p> <p>Join the free PsyBlog mailing list. No spam, ever.</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.spring.org.uk/2026/11/couples-life-hard.php" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9607"> <h2>#9607. Creamy Stovetop Mac and Cheese</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://pinchofyum.com/tachyon/Hero-Option-1-Panera-Mac-and-Cheese-scaled.jpg" alt="Creamy Stovetop Mac and Cheese" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>Thick and creamy mac and cheese – made on the stovetop! Everyone loves this one!</p> <p>Published by Lindsay Ostrom on November 11, 2026</p> <p>Thick, creamy, and I might even say Panera-style in its creamy, cheesy, velvety glory.</p> <p>This summer, my daughter and my husband biked 50+ miles to raise money for frogs (I know, can’t make this up, but stick with me). We had a little welcome home party at the end of the bike ride, and I made this mac and cheese for 25 people at that party. Multiple friends came up and asked me for the recipe.</p> <p>Since then, I’ve made this several more times, always when we have friends for dinner or I’m feeding a big group of people.</p> <p>So in my mind, this is a party mac and cheese. You can serve it to a lot of people, and mostly everyone will love it.</p> <p>(Pictured here with the BBQ meatballs that I made for our friends last night! So yum.)</p> <p>When I do this for a group of people, I’ll do a couple things ahead of time:</p> <p>Then when it’s time to assemble, I reheat the bechamel, add the cheese, and stir the noodles in. A bit of warm water at the end helps it stay loose and creamy!</p> <p>My favorite cheese lately has been the cheddar and Gruyere blend blocks that you can buy at ALDI or Trader Joe’s, but I also love some straight cheddar or even a few slices of American for a milder, creamier finish.</p> <p>It’s just uncluttered, creamy, comforting homemade mac and cheese. Hope you love it!</p> <p>Pasta, cheese, butter, milk – all the essentials!</p> <p>Cook your noodles and set aside (I love to use classic elbow macaroni!).</p> <p>Melt butter, add flour, and whisk until nice and bubbly!</p> <p>Go slowly and whisk after each little bit. Stir stir stir until it’s nice and smooth and thickened.</p> <p>Chef’s choice, but I like Gruyere and mild cheddar!</p> <p>Add your noodles and bring it all together!</p> <p>That’s it! Cheesy, comforting, and so good.</p> <p>5 Stars 4 Stars 3 Stars 2 Stars 1 Star</p> <p>Thick and creamy mac and cheese! People always ask me for this recipe. We call it party mac and cheese because it’s perfect for a crowd!</p> <p>This will thicken up as it rests, so it is best to serve almost immediately.</p> <p>If you want to prep it ahead (which I do quite a bit, being that it’s party mac and cheese) – I cook the noodles ahead, grate the cheese ahead, and even make the bechamel sauce with the flour, butter, and milk. Then, right before serving, I re-warm the sauce (adding water and whisking to bring make it smooth again), gently melt the cheese in, and toss the noodles in the sauce.</p> <p>Keywords: stovetop mac and cheese, easy mac and cheese, panera mac and cheese, mac and cheese recipe</p> <p>I love hearing from you!
